soru: What is a good example of safe (defensive) driving?
secenekler: Driving fast in poor visibility conditions
Adapting speed to the road surface
Always driving very slowly
Braking hard and often
aciklama: Defensive driving means being aware of risks. Adapting speed to the road surface is a fundamental rule.

soru: What is counted as the 'Carriageway'?
secenekler: The road itself, excluding the shoulder and cycle path
The entire road including the cycle path
The entire road including the shoulder
aciklama: The carriageway is the part of the road intended for vehicle traffic and does not include the shoulder or cycle path.

soru: Can you change lanes in the situation shown in the picture?
secenekler: Yes, if there is no risk, the line is only a recommendation
No, I am not allowed to cross a solid line
Yes, the line only separates the lanes
aciklama: As a main rule, you are not allowed to cross a solid line. Not even a tyre may touch the line.

soru: What do the basic traffic rules generally describe?
secenekler: Whether I have right of way or not
Which laws apply in traffic
How I should think and behave in traffic
Which lane I should use in roundabouts
aciklama: The basic traffic rules describe what 'mindset' and approach should prevail in traffic.

soru: What is the best way to avoid ending up in risky situations?
secenekler: Drive often in the dark
Use engine braking only in emergencies
Always drive very slowly
Maintain good safety margins
aciklama: The best way to avoid risks is 'defensive driving'. This means always keeping sufficient safety distances.

soru: Must a lane always be marked with road lines?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: Lanes are not always marked with road lines. If two four-wheeled vehicles can fit next to each other, it counts as two lanes.

soru: What is the basic speed limit outside built-up areas?
secenekler: 50 km/h
70 km/h
90 km/h
110 km/h
aciklama: There are basic speed limits to facilitate where signs are missing: 50 km/h in built-up areas and 70 km/h outside built-up areas.

soru: How do you best apply safe driving?
secenekler: I plan my driving, show respect for other road users, and do not take unnecessary risks
I always keep a lower speed than the speed limit
I always strictly follow traffic rules
aciklama: For traffic interaction to work well, it is important to plan your driving and drive clearly and safely. This is called defensive driving.

soru: You are driving at 48 km/h on a road with a 70 km/h limit and heavy traffic. A queue forms behind you. Are you driving correctly?
secenekler: No, I am obstructing other traffic by driving so slowly
Yes, it is good to drive slowly and carefully
No, I am not allowed to drive more than 20 km/h below the speed limit
Yes, there is no rule on how slowly I am allowed to drive
aciklama: One of the basic traffic rules is not to unnecessarily obstruct or disturb traffic. If road and visibility conditions are good, you should not drive unnecessarily slowly.

soru: In which case are you allowed to cross the solid line?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, only in case C
No
aciklama: As a main rule, you are not allowed to cross a solid line. There is one exception: if there is a dashed line immediately to the right of the solid line (as in case B), you may cross it.

soru: When should the horn be used?
secenekler: When I am angry at other drivers
Every time I overtake
If necessary to prevent an accident
aciklama: The horn should be used to prevent an accident or to draw attention from other road users who have not seen you. It should not be used in anger or to greet.

soru: How do you best avoid ending up in risky situations?
secenekler: Drive often in the dark
Use engine braking only in emergencies
Always drive slowly
Maintain good safety margins
aciklama: To avoid risky situations, you should drive defensively: stay calm, plan your driving, and keep large safety margins.

soru: You are driving on an open gravel area used as parking. What applies?
secenekler: There are no specific rules for such open areas
No vehicle has right of way, it is mutual interaction
The right-hand rule should be applied
aciklama: The right-hand rule should also be applied in squares, parking areas, and similar open spaces when two vehicles meet.

soru: You are going straight ahead and a cyclist is approaching slowly from the right. Which statement is correct?
secenekler: The cyclist has right of way against me because I am going straight
I have right of way against the cyclist because it is coming from the right
Since I am driving a motor vehicle, the cyclist has right of way against me
I have right of way against the cyclist according to the exit rule
aciklama: In intersections without signs, the right-hand rule applies. According to the right-hand rule, you must give way to traffic from the right, including cyclists.

soru: The silver car is coming out of a petrol station. What applies at the intersection?
secenekler: The silver car must give way to me according to the exit rule
According to the right-hand rule, I must give way
According to the exit rule, I must give way
aciklama: The exit rule applies when you drive out from a parking lot, petrol station, or property. According to this rule, you must give way to traffic on the road. The silver car must therefore wait.

soru: You are going straight ahead. Does the right-hand rule apply in any of the intersections?
secenekler: Yes, but only in case A
Yes, but only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: The right-hand rule applies in intersections where no other traffic sign or rule exists. Since there are no give way or main road signs in either case, the right-hand rule applies in both.

soru: Does the right-hand rule apply in a roundabout?
secenekler: No
Yes, unless otherwise directed
aciklama: In roundabouts, the right-hand rule does not apply. Drivers entering the roundabout must give way to vehicles already in the roundabout.

soru: In which situation does the right-hand rule apply?
secenekler: When I drive out from a petrol station
When I am on a main road and approaching an intersection
When I approach an intersection without signs within a built-up area
When I drive out from a parking lot
aciklama: The exit rule applies at petrol stations and parking lots. On a main road, the right-hand rule does not apply. The right-hand rule applies in intersections without signs or a main road.

soru: You are approaching an intersection and will turn right onto the main road. A cyclist is coming from the left on the main road. What applies?
secenekler: The cyclist must give way to me according to the right-hand rule
The cyclist must give way to me because the right of way only applies to motor vehicles
I must give way to the cyclist
aciklama: When you enter a main road, you must give way to all vehicles on the main road, regardless of whether it is a motor vehicle or bicycle. The cyclist has priority.

soru: You are approaching an intersection with this traffic sign. Which is correct?
secenekler: I must stop before entering the intersecting road
All traffic on the intersecting road must give way to me
The right-hand rule applies at this sign
I must give way to all traffic on the intersecting road
aciklama: The give way sign means you must yield to all traffic on the intersecting road (from the right or left). There is no stop requirement, but you must stop if necessary.

soru: You are driving on a main road and approaching an intersection. What should you consider?
secenekler: Since I am driving on a main road, I don't need to be aware of crossing traffic
I must give way to crossing traffic
Even though I am on a main road, I must be attentive because crossing traffic may come
aciklama: Traffic on the main road has priority, but you must always be alert and prepared for other drivers to miss you or break the rules.

soru: The pictures show the back of traffic signs. Which option shows the 'STOP' sign?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: The STOP sign is the only sign in the world that is octagonal. This allows drivers to recognise it even from behind and understand that other vehicles have a stop obligation.

soru: Sometimes the stop line at a STOP sign can be difficult to see. Where should you stop then?
secenekler: At least three metres before the intersecting road
One metre into the intersecting road to show others that I am coming out
Immediately before the intersecting road (before driving into it)
Level with the STOP sign
aciklama: If a stop line exists, you should stop there. If the line is missing or invisible, you should stop immediately before the intersecting road (where you have full visibility).

soru: Is the main road sign placed before or after intersections?
secenekler: After
Before
aciklama: The main road sign is usually repeated AFTER each intersection. The purpose is that newly arrived road users should also understand they are on a main road.

soru: You are approaching an intersection with this combination of traffic signs (STOP and Four-way stop). What applies?
secenekler: All vehicles must stop and show mutual respect/politeness towards each other in the intersection
I must first stop, then according to the right-hand rule give way to traffic from the right
I only need to stop if there are other vehicles in the intersection
aciklama: In intersections with four-way stop, all vehicles from all directions must stop. As a rule, the one who first arrived at the intersection and stopped, also gets to pass first.

soru: You are approaching the intersection in the picture. Should you inform the traffic on the intersecting road that you have right of way?
secenekler: Yes, by slowing down well before the intersection
No, it could lead to misunderstandings
Yes, by honking before entering the intersecting road
No, drivers on the intersecting road already know that I have right of way
aciklama: It is important to plan your driving and clearly show your intentions in traffic. Therefore, you should slow down in good time to show that you have right of way and are prepared to stop.

soru: You are going to turn left. Which is correct?
secenekler: Oncoming traffic must give way and should brake to facilitate my turn
I must give way to oncoming traffic
There is no right of way, it is a shared responsibility
aciklama: According to the turning rule, when turning left at an intersection, you must not obstruct oncoming traffic going straight or turning right, and you must give way to them.

soru: Which rule applies in the intersection shown in the picture?
secenekler: The exit rule
All other vehicles in the intersection must give way to me
The right-hand rule
aciklama: When you drive out from a pedestrian zone, the 'exit rule' always applies. This means you must give way to all vehicles and pedestrians on the road before driving out.

soru: You are going straight ahead in the intersection. How should you act?
secenekler: I wait and let the cyclist pass first, because it is signalling that it is going to turn
I go first, but am prepared to brake because the cyclist is signalling a turn
Since the right-hand rule applies, I let the cyclist pass
I go first because cyclists must give way to motor vehicles
aciklama: According to the turning rule, left-turning traffic must give way to oncoming traffic. But the cyclist may break the rule, so you should be prepared to brake.

soru: You have just fuelled up and are about to drive out from the petrol station. What applies?
secenekler: I only need to give way to traffic from the right according to the right-hand rule
Traffic on the road must give way to me according to the exit rule
I must give way to all traffic on the road
aciklama: When driving out from a petrol station, the 'exit rule' applies. According to this rule, you must give way to all traffic on the road.

soru: You are going to turn right at the intersection. The oncoming blue car is signalling a left turn. What applies?
secenekler: I must give way, so I let the blue car pass first
It is mutual interaction since no one is coming from the right
I should pass first because the blue car must give way to me
aciklama: According to the turning rule, a driver who turns left at an intersection must give way to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.

soru: You are going straight ahead and a green car is approaching from the right. Does the exit rule apply in any of the cases?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: In both cases, the green car is driving out from a property. According to the exit rule, those driving out from a property must give way to all traffic on the road.

soru: In both cases, a green car is approaching from the right. Does the exit rule apply in any of the cases?
secenekler: Yes, but only in case A
Yes, but only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: In parking areas and entrances from private roads, the right-hand rule applies unless otherwise stated. Therefore, the exit rule does not apply in either case, but the right-hand rule applies.

soru: What applies when you drive from an acceleration lane onto the motorway?
secenekler: All traffic on the motorway must give way to me
I must give way to all traffic on the motorway
It is mutual interaction
aciklama: At motorway on-ramps, neither those in the acceleration lane nor those on the motorway have sole priority. It is a mutual interaction.

soru: You are driving on a road with a 70 km/h limit. Ahead of you, you see a bus that has dropped off passengers and is about to pull out. What applies?
secenekler: I must always give way to the bus regardless of the speed limit
On this road, the bus driver must give way to me before pulling out
Before the bus driver pulls out, I must give way to it
Bus drivers must always give way to me regardless of the speed limit
aciklama: If the speed limit is 60 km/h or higher (here 70 km/h), the bus driver must give way to you when pulling out from the bus stop.

soru: You are driving at 45 km/h on a road with a 50 km/h limit. You are about to pass a bus standing at a stop. How should you act?
secenekler: I should slow down and be prepared to brake at any time
I should stop behind the bus and wait until it drives away
I should increase speed to 50 km/h to quickly pass the bus, but be careful
aciklama: When passing a stationary bus, there is always a risk that a pedestrian may suddenly walk out in front of the bus. Therefore, you should slow down and be prepared.

soru: You are in an acceleration lane. What should you do?
secenekler: I must stop before entering the motorway
I must give way to all traffic on the motorway
I should adjust my speed to merge into a suitable gap without disturbing traffic
aciklama: The purpose of the acceleration lane is for you to adjust your speed to the traffic flow on the motorway and safely merge into a suitable gap.

soru: Must you always give way to and facilitate the passage of emergency vehicles such as ambulances?
secenekler: Yes, always
No, I don't need to give way if the emergency vehicle does not have blue lights or sirens on
aciklama: You are only required to give way to and facilitate the passage of emergency vehicles when they have blue lights or sirens activated.

soru: What should you do when you end up in a traffic queue?
secenekler: I should stop so that I do not block crossing traffic
I should always keep the same distance to the vehicle in front
I should drive as close as possible to the vehicle in front so that the queue looks shorter
aciklama: The blockage rule means that in heavy traffic, you must not block intersections or pedestrian crossings.

soru: You are going to turn right and the traffic light shows a green right arrow, but underneath there is a 'Give way' sign. What applies?
secenekler: Despite the green arrow, I must wait because the main signal is red
The traffic sign takes precedence over the traffic light, so I must stop and give way
I may drive because the green arrow is lit and traffic lights take precedence over signs
aciklama: When the traffic light shows a green arrow, you may drive, and you do not need to consider any give way sign underneath. Traffic lights take precedence over signs.

soru: Which instruction or rule always has the highest priority in traffic?
secenekler: Traffic lights
A police officer's signal
Traffic signs
The right-hand rule
aciklama: In Swedish traffic, the hierarchy is: 1. Police officer's signal, 2. Traffic signals (lights), 3. Traffic signs, 4. General rules.

soru: You see that the traffic light shows red and yellow at the same time. What does it mean?
secenekler: The light will soon change to red
The traffic signal is broken
The light will soon change to green
aciklama: In Swedish traffic lights, red and yellow signal at the same time means that the light will soon change to green.

soru: You are on a main road and approaching an intersection where the traffic light is flashing yellow. What applies?
secenekler: The other vehicles in the intersection must give way to me
I must give way to all other vehicles
I must give way to vehicles from the right
aciklama: Flashing yellow light means the traffic light is out of order. Since you are on a main road, you have priority.

soru: You are driving in the right lane and are going to turn right. The traffic light is red, but next to it there is a 'Give way' sign. What should you do?
secenekler: I must wait for a green light before driving
Since traffic on the cross street has a red light, I have priority
I don't need to wait for green, but I must give way to traffic on the intersecting road
aciklama: The traffic light only applies to those going straight. For the right lane, there is no traffic light, so you may turn according to the give way sign.

soru: In which of the cases shown in the picture is a left turn allowed?
secenekler: Only in case A
Only in case B
In both case A and B
aciklama: Left turn is allowed in both cases. With a green arrow, you may turn directly; with a green light, you must give way to oncoming traffic.

soru: You are approaching the intersection in the picture and are going straight ahead. The traffic lights are off (not working). Do you have to give way to traffic in the intersection?
secenekler: No, traffic in the intersection must give way to me
Yes, I must give way to traffic from both the right and left
Yes, only to traffic from the left
Yes, only to traffic from the right
aciklama: If the lights are not working, the signs apply. Since there is a 'Give way' sign, you must give way to traffic from both directions.

soru: You see a STOP sign under a traffic light that shows green. Must you stop before driving?
secenekler: Yes, if there is a STOP sign, I must always stop
No, the STOP sign does not apply when the traffic light shows green
I only need to stop if there are other vehicles in the intersection
aciklama: As long as the traffic light is working, you should not consider STOP or give way signs underneath. Traffic lights take precedence.

soru: What applies in the intersection after this traffic sign, unless otherwise stated?
secenekler: I must give way to traffic from the right
All crossing traffic must give way to me
I must give way to traffic from the left
I must give way to all crossing traffic
aciklama: Sign: 'End of main road'. If no other signs exist, the right-hand rule applies.

soru: You are going straight ahead. Does the right-hand rule apply in any of the intersections?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: In both cases (A and B), there are no signs, therefore the right-hand rule applies.

soru: Which of the following is an example of mature traffic behaviour?
secenekler: Facilitating for someone who is changing lanes
Always driving slowly
Only following traffic rules when police are nearby
aciklama: The correct approach is to always be considerate towards other drivers and facilitate in traffic. Always driving slowly can disrupt traffic; speed should be adapted to conditions. Traffic rules should be followed regardless of whether police are present or not.

soru: Which of the following is an example of mature traffic behaviour?
secenekler: Facilitating for someone who is changing lanes
Always driving slowly
Only following traffic rules when police are nearby
aciklama: The correct approach is to always be considerate towards other drivers and facilitate in traffic. Always driving slowly can disrupt traffic; speed should be adapted to conditions. Traffic rules should be followed regardless of whether police are present or not.

soru: You are driving the green car. The red truck is parked at the roadside due to work. Is it allowed to cross the solid centre line to overtake the truck?
secenekler: No, I must stop and wait until the truck driver is finished
Yes, if I do not obstruct oncoming traffic
Yes, but only if I use hazard lights
aciklama: If an obstacle must be passed, it is permitted to cross a solid line. The truck that is working counts as an obstacle. You may pass as long as you do not obstruct oncoming traffic.

soru: You are in a parking lot. You are going straight ahead and an orange car is approaching from the right. Which rule applies?
secenekler: I go first because the orange car has to give way
I let the orange car pass because I have to give way according to the right-hand rule
I slow down and see what the orange car does because this is a mutual interaction
aciklama: In parking lots, the right-hand rule applies. You must give way to vehicles from the right. The orange car therefore has priority.

soru: You encounter this sign combination. Which of the following is correct?
secenekler: I must stop immediately before the railway track
I only need to stop if a train is coming
If there is no stop line, I must stop 10 metres before the track
If there is no stop line, I must stop level with the STOP sign
aciklama: Signs: 'Railway crossing' and 'Stop obligation'. Where there is a STOP sign, you must stop immediately before the road or track. You also have to give way to all vehicles (or trains).

soru: When you are driving on a public road that is not a main road, in which situation does the right-hand rule apply?
secenekler: When a private road crosses the public road
When I pass an exit from a petrol station
When I pass an exit from a parking lot
When the road crosses a main road
aciklama: The right-hand rule applies at intersections and where private roads meet public roads, unless otherwise stated. At exits from petrol stations and parking lots, the exit rule applies, i.e. the one driving out must give way.

soru: What is the basic speed limit within built-up areas?
secenekler: 30 km/h
50 km/h
60 km/h
70 km/h
aciklama: The basic speed limit within built-up areas is 50 km/h, outside built-up areas 70 km/h.

soru: You are approaching a traffic light that is flashing yellow. Then the light changes to a steady yellow. What should you do?
secenekler: Continue driving, because it will soon turn green
Look at signs or other markers because the traffic light is probably broken
Stop, because it will soon turn red
aciklama: Steady yellow light means it will soon turn red and you must stop. With flashing yellow, signs (give way, stop) or the right-hand rule apply. But when it changes to steady yellow, it is a warning for red.

soru: Which instruction must you follow first and foremost?
secenekler: A police officer's signal
Give way sign
STOP sign
Traffic light
aciklama: The priority order in traffic is: 1. Police officer's signal, 2. Traffic signals (lights), 3. Traffic signs, 4. General traffic rules. The police always have the highest priority.

soru: How should you apply the basic rules when driving in a built-up area with street lighting?
secenekler: Use high beams to see better in the dark and avoid danger
Use high beams to hurry pedestrians at crossings
Adjust speed when there are children nearby
Use the horn to speed up vehicles in front
aciklama: The basic traffic rules are: show care and attention, do not unnecessarily disturb or obstruct others, show respect for residents and the environment. Be extra careful towards children, elderly and disabled people.

soru: What applies when there are two parallel solid lines in the middle of the road?
secenekler: It is allowed to cross the lines only when overtaking
It is not allowed to cross the lines
Only lane traffic (buses etc.) may cross the lines
The lines only mark the lanes (free to cross)
aciklama: As a main rule, you are not allowed to cross a solid line. Not even a tyre may touch the line. Exceptions only apply for passing an obstacle, lack of space at intersections, or entering/exiting a property.

soru: You are driving quite slowly and notice that a long queue of cars has formed behind you. What should you do?
secenekler: Brake lightly to turn on the brake lights and reduce the risk of rear-end collision
Pull into the nearest suitable lay-by so that the cars behind can pass
Do nothing, it is normal for queues to form
aciklama: You should not unnecessarily obstruct traffic. When you drive too slowly and block traffic, it is safest to pull into a lay-by or similar to let the cars behind pass.

soru: You are approaching this intersection on a main road. What should you do?
secenekler: Continue driving and trust that the driver on the right will brake
Brake and let the right car enter the main road
Continue driving but be prepared to act at any time
aciklama: Since you are on a main road, the green car from the right has to give way. But you must always be prepared for the driver not having seen you.

soru: What applies when you change lanes from the acceleration lane onto the motorway?
secenekler: I must give way to all traffic on the motorway
All traffic on the motorway must give way to me
It is mutual interaction
aciklama: Neither you in the acceleration lane nor those on the motorway have sole right of way. It is mutual interaction. You in the acceleration lane should make a safe merge, and those on the motorway should facilitate by adjusting speed.

soru: You have just got your driving licence. What approach should you have to minimise the risk of accidents in traffic?
secenekler: Drive with large safety margins and defensively
Drive in difficult traffic conditions to develop my skills
Always drive well below the speed limit
Only drive on roads I know
aciklama: For new drivers, the safest way is 'defensive' driving with large safety margins. It provides room for mistakes.

soru: You are driving at 50 km/h. What should you do in this situation?
secenekler: Continue driving, the bus gives no signal
Honk to warn invisible pedestrians
Brake and wait until the bus leaves
Take your foot off the accelerator and be prepared to stop
aciklama: The greatest risk is that pedestrians suddenly walk out in front of the bus. It is difficult to spot them in time, so you must be prepared to brake.

soru: How should you best adjust your speed in traffic?
secenekler: Always drive at the applicable speed limit
Drive slowly through all curves
Without exceeding the speed limit, adjust speed to the traffic situation
Exceed the speed limit if necessary to speed up the vehicle in front
aciklama: You must never exceed the speed limit. But for safe driving, you should adjust your speed not only according to signs, but also according to visibility, road conditions and traffic intensity.

soru: When should you use the horn?
secenekler: When I am in a hurry and want the vehicle in front to drive faster
When I see a friend and want to greet them
When I am overtaking
When necessary to prevent a dangerous situation
aciklama: The horn should only be used to prevent danger and warn other road users who have not seen you. It is forbidden to use the horn to greet or to speed up others.

soru: You are approaching an intersection without signs in a residential area. You are going straight ahead, which rule applies?
secenekler: I must give way to all traffic in the intersection
I must give way to traffic from the left
I must give way to oncoming traffic
I must give way to traffic from the right
aciklama: This is not a main road and there are no traffic signs. In such cases, the 'Right-hand rule' applies, i.e. you must give way to traffic from the right.

soru: You are driving on a main road and see in the rear-view mirror a fire engine with blue lights and sirens. What should you do?
secenekler: Drive as close to the centre line as possible
Slow down and pull over, but do not stop because I am on a main road
Continue driving as usual
Slow down, pull over, and stop if necessary
aciklama: You must always give way to emergency vehicles with blue lights and sirens (fire engine, ambulance, police). This means you should pull over and stop if necessary.

soru: You are going to turn left at the intersection. The oncoming turquoise car is going straight ahead. Which rule applies?
secenekler: The turquoise car must give way to me according to the turning rule
According to the right-hand rule, I must give way to the turquoise car
According to the turning rule, I must give way to the turquoise car
According to the right-hand rule, the turquoise car must give way to me
aciklama: When you turn left, you cross oncoming traffic. According to the 'Turning rule', the one turning left must give way to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.

soru: You are about to drive out from a property (house/plot) and join the road. What should you do?
secenekler: The right-hand rule applies, I give way to traffic from the left
The right-hand rule applies, I give way to traffic from the right
The exit rule applies, I give way to all traffic on the road
aciklama: When driving out from a property, parking lot, petrol station or similar, the 'Exit rule' applies. You then have to give way to all vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists on the road.

soru: You are going to turn left at the intersection shown in the picture. The light is green. What should you do?
secenekler: Turn immediately because oncoming traffic has red
Drive forward but give way to oncoming traffic
Turn immediately because oncoming traffic must give way to me
aciklama: Green light means you may enter the intersection. But with a green light, oncoming traffic also has green. According to the 'Turning rule', you must give way to oncoming vehicles when turning left.

soru: What shows that you are driving defensively?
secenekler: I accelerate and brake a lot
I drive impulsively and am prepared for anything
I always drive 10 km/h below the speed limit
I brake in good time and smoothly before red lights
aciklama: Defensive driving means planned driving, not being in a hurry, smooth driving and maintaining large safety margins. Braking smoothly and in good time before red lights increases safety.

soru: You are approaching this intersection. Which of the following is correct?
secenekler: I must give way to all traffic on the intersecting road
I only have to give way to traffic from the right
I must stop before entering the intersecting road
aciklama: The give way sign means you must yield to all traffic on the intersecting road. There is no stop obligation, but you must slow down and stop if the road is occupied.

soru: What is called the 'Carriageway'?
secenekler: The entire road including the cycle path
The entire road including the shoulder
The part of the road intended for vehicle traffic, excluding the shoulder and cycle path
aciklama: The carriageway is the part of the road intended for vehicle traffic. Cycle paths and shoulders are not counted as carriageway.

soru: What should you adjust your speed according to?
secenekler: Only according to the speed signs on the road
According to the distance you can see and stop within
According to a speed that is high enough not to disturb traffic behind
According to what time of day it is
aciklama: The basic rule for safe driving is to adjust speed according to visibility conditions. You should always be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

soru: The silver car is coming out of a petrol station. Which rule applies at the intersection?
secenekler: According to the exit rule, I must give way to the silver car
According to the exit rule, the silver car must give way to me
According to the right-hand rule, I must give way to the silver car
aciklama: At exits from petrol stations, parking lots or properties, the 'Exit rule' applies. The one driving out (the silver car) must give way to other traffic.

soru: What does the solid yellow line at the kerb mean?
secenekler: I may stop briefly but not park
It is forbidden to stop and park here
I may park for a maximum of 5 minutes
aciklama: Solid yellow line means 'No stopping and no parking'. It is therefore forbidden to both stop and park.

soru: Is it allowed to stop here to drop off a passenger, as the green car is doing?
secenekler: Yes, but only briefly and temporarily
Yes, but only if I do not obstruct other traffic
No
Yes, because this is within a built-up area
aciklama: It is absolutely forbidden to stop or park within an intersection or within 10 metres before or after an intersection. The green car is less than 10 metres from the intersection, so it is not allowed to stop.

soru: Which of the following is correct regarding parking rules?
secenekler: I may not park within 10 metres after a pedestrian crossing
I may not park so that other road users are obstructed or exposed to danger
It is completely forbidden to park on hills
aciklama: The basic principle in Swedish traffic rules is not to obstruct or expose others to danger. It is forbidden to park at least 10 metres BEFORE a pedestrian crossing, but immediately after is allowed.

soru: Is it allowed to park as the green car is doing?
secenekler: Yes, because all wheels are within the parking lines
No, because the car is parked on the left side in the direction of travel
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, you must always park on the right side in the direction of travel. It is forbidden to park on the left side, against the direction of travel. Exceptions are one-way streets.

soru: If you do not have a special permit, is it allowed to stop at a disabled parking space to unload goods?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: Without a special disabled parking permit, it is absolutely forbidden to load or unload goods at these spaces. The only exception is dropping off or picking up passengers.

soru: Which of the following applies to the dashed yellow line at the kerb?
secenekler: I may park here but the wheels may not be on the pavement
It is completely forbidden to park and stop here
I may park here for a maximum of 24 hours
I may stop here (for passengers/goods) but not park
aciklama: Dashed yellow line at the kerb means 'No parking'. You may stop temporarily for passengers or goods, but you may not park.

soru: What is the most important thing to think about when parking your car?
secenekler: Make sure the wheels are straight
Make sure the car does not roll away
Make sure all valuables are with me
Make sure all lights are off
aciklama: The most important responsibility after parking is to ensure that the car is stationary. Especially on hills, you must apply the handbrake and put the car in gear.

soru: You have just parked your car (the turquoise one). The whole car is within the parking lines, but you have parked so close to the silver car that its driver cannot open the door. Is this parking method legal?
secenekler: Yes, because my car is completely within the parking lines
No, because I am obstructing the driver of the silver car
aciklama: Even if your car is within the lines, you may not park so that another driver is prevented from getting into their car. Courtesy and not obstructing take precedence over the lines.

soru: In which situation should you refrain from using the handbrake and instead only put the car in gear when parking?
secenekler: When it is warm and humid
When it is cold and dry
When it is warm and dry
When it is cold and humid
aciklama: According to the Swedish driving licence book: When it is cold and humid, there is a risk that the handbrake mechanism may freeze. Then it is safer to only put the car in gear.

soru: Which of the following is correct regarding parking rules?
secenekler: I may park 30 metres before a railway crossing
I may park 30 metres after a railway crossing
I may park 10 metres before a pedestrian crossing
I may park within 10 metres after a pedestrian crossing
aciklama: It is forbidden to park 30 metres before and after railway crossings. At pedestrian crossings, it is only forbidden to park 10 metres before. Immediately after the crossing, it is allowed to park.

soru: In both cases, there are 2 metres between the red car and the solid white line. Is it allowed for the red car to stop there?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: Normally, there should be at least 3 metres between the vehicle and a solid line. But in case B, where there is a dashed line in between, the distance can be less than 3 metres because vehicles behind can legally use that lane.

soru: You are driving in a tunnel. Which of the following is correct?
secenekler: I may stop if I flash my lights
I may stop only on the shoulder
It is absolutely forbidden to stop
I may stop if I turn on the hazard lights
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, it is absolutely forbidden to stop or park in tunnels and underpasses.

soru: In any of the cases where the yellow car is parked, is it allowed to stop to drop off a passenger?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: It is forbidden to stop 10 metres before a cycle crossing (case A) because it obscures visibility for traffic from behind. But immediately after the crossing (case B), it is allowed to stop.

soru: You are going to park near a bus stop. At what distance from the stop is it allowed to park?
secenekler: 10 metres before and 10 metres after
30 metres before and 30 metres after
5 metres before and 20 metres after
20 metres before and 5 metres after
aciklama: For buses to be able to stop smoothly, it is absolutely forbidden to park 20 metres before and 5 metres after a bus stop.

soru: In which of the following places is it NOT ALLOWED to stop, even to drop off a passenger?
secenekler: Where the car obscures a traffic sign
On a main road
At a bus stop
In front of an exit from a property or garage
aciklama: It is absolutely forbidden to stop or park where your vehicle obscures a traffic sign or traffic light for other drivers.

soru: Is it allowed to stop at a tram stop?
secenekler: No, absolutely forbidden
Yes, only to drop off and pick up passengers, without obstructing tram traffic
Yes, only to load/unload goods, without obstructing tram traffic
Yes, for a maximum of 5 minutes for any purpose
aciklama: The same rules apply for tram stops as for bus stops. Parking is forbidden 20 m before and 5 m after, but temporary stop for boarding/alighting is allowed.

soru: What does the traffic sign with a round red border, blue background and a red cross (X) mean?
secenekler: I may park here for a maximum of 10 minutes
I may only stop here for loading
I may neither park nor stop here
It indicates that the road is prohibited for passenger cars
aciklama: The sign with a red cross (X) means 'No stopping and no parking'. It is forbidden to stop even to drop off passengers.

soru: Is it allowed to park on a main road?
secenekler: Yes, if the speed limit is 70 km/h or lower
Yes, if the speed limit is 50 km/h or lower
Yes, if I do not obstruct other traffic
No
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, it is completely forbidden to park on a main road.

soru: When does it count as having parked your car?
secenekler: When I stop to pick up a passenger
When I stop to quickly withdraw money from an ATM
When I stop to unload a bag
When I turn off the engine at a red light
aciklama: All types of voluntary stops for purposes other than boarding/alighting or loading (e.g. withdrawing money) are immediately counted as 'parking'.

soru: In which situation is it not allowed to stop on a main road?
secenekler: When I stop to talk on the mobile phone
When I stop to drop off a passenger
When I stop to give way to a pedestrian at a pedestrian crossing
aciklama: Dropping off passengers or stopping for traffic safety reasons is allowed. But stopping to talk on the phone is not such an exception and violates the parking ban on main roads.

soru: What is a parking disc?
secenekler: A safety device against theft
A device that indicates the arrival time at a parking space
A steering wheel lock used when parking
aciklama: The parking disc is a mechanical device placed in the windscreen to show when the car was parked, and is used for free but time-limited parking.

soru: You park your car on 1 January at 5:00 PM. You plan to leave it parked until 10:00 AM the next day. This traffic sign is on the street. Where is it allowed to park?
secenekler: On the side of the street with even house numbers
On the side of the street with odd house numbers
It is forbidden to park on both sides
It is allowed to park on both sides
aciklama: At midnight, it becomes 2 January (even date). According to the date rule, it is forbidden to park on the even side on even dates, so you must park on the odd side.

soru: You park your car at a place with this traffic sign on a Saturday at 5:00 PM. When must you move your car at the latest?
secenekler: Saturday at 12:00 AM
Sunday at 5:00 PM
Sunday at 12:00 AM
Monday at 12:00 AM
aciklama: On standard 'P' signs, the 24-hour limit does not apply on weekends. The time limit starts on Monday at 00:00. With 24 hours of right, you may stay until Monday at 12:00 AM (midnight).

soru: Which traffic sign prohibits parking on odd dates?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign A: With the single white line inside, it indicates that parking is forbidden on odd dates.

soru: You park your car on a Saturday at 6:00 PM. When is the latest you must collect your car?
secenekler: Saturday at 8:00 PM
Sunday at 12:00 PM
Monday at 8:00 AM
Monday at 10:00 AM
aciklama: Since you parked after the restriction time on Saturday evening, Sunday is free. The restriction starts on Monday at 8:00 AM and with a 2-hour parking right, you must collect your car by 10:00 AM on Monday at the latest.

soru: What is a parking attendant's main task?
secenekler: Ensure parking rules are followed
Collect parking fees
Check that vehicles keep to the speed limit
Protect parked cars from theft
aciklama: The parking attendant's primary task is to monitor that established parking rules and time limits are complied with, in order to maintain traffic flow.

soru: What applies at a pedestrian crossing?
secenekler: I must always stop before the pedestrian crossing before proceeding
Cyclists and pedestrians must give way to me
I must be prepared to stop for cyclists or pedestrians
aciklama: When approaching a pedestrian crossing, you should always be prepared to stop and give priority to pedestrians and cyclists who are about to or are crossing. It is not always a stop obligation, but you must adjust your speed and stop if necessary for a safe passage.

soru: Is it allowed to drive onto the road in the picture to pick up a friend at a hotel located along the road?
secenekler: Yes, but I may drive at a maximum of 30 km/h
No
Yes, but only at walking speed
aciklama: A pedestrian street is normally prohibited for motor traffic, only crossing is allowed. Exceptions are made for picking up hotel guests, delivering goods, or transporting sick/disabled persons. Then you may only drive at walking speed (approx. 5-7 km/h) and must give way to pedestrians.

soru: In the picture, a pedestrian is waiting at a pedestrian crossing. Do you have to give way?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: This is a controlled pedestrian crossing with traffic signals. Since the traffic light shows red for the pedestrian, you do not have to give way to them.

soru: Is it allowed to park as the vehicle is doing in these situations?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: In case A, the car is parked on a pedestrian street, and in case B, in a pedestrian zone. It is not allowed to park in either pedestrian streets or pedestrian zones. Exception: only in specially marked parking spaces.

soru: You have stopped at a red light at a pedestrian crossing. When it turns green, there are still children on the crossing. What should you do?
secenekler: Start rolling slowly and wave at them to hurry up
Wait until everyone has crossed before you start driving
Start driving because the light is green
Honk to make them hurry so that traffic is not held up
aciklama: Even if the light has turned green, you must wait until all pedestrians have had time to cross the crossing before you start driving.

soru: You are approaching an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing. A pedestrian is about to cross. Is it appropriate to try to make eye contact with the pedestrian?
secenekler: No, it is better to wave at the pedestrian to cross
No, it creates a false sense of security for the pedestrian
Yes, it reduces the risk of misunderstandings
aciklama: At uncontrolled pedestrian crossings, eye contact with other road users is very important to avoid misunderstandings. Through eye contact, you can better understand whether the pedestrian has seen you and their intentions.

soru: You are approaching a pedestrian crossing where a pedestrian is standing on a traffic island. What should you do?
secenekler: I should slow down but can continue because the pedestrian is on the traffic island
I should slow down but can continue because the crossing is protected by the island and the pedestrian must give way to me
I should slow down, stop, and let the pedestrian cross
aciklama: The crossing is uncontrolled, meaning there is no traffic light or police. Therefore, you have to give way to all pedestrians who are on or are about to step onto the crossing. You must slow down and stop to show that you intend to let the pedestrian cross.

soru: You are driving behind a cyclist on a straight road. Is it allowed to overtake the cyclist when approaching an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: Immediately before uncontrolled pedestrian crossings, there is generally a no-overtaking rule. This prohibition also applies to overtaking two-wheeled vehicles such as bicycles.

soru: A pedestrian is approaching from the right. How should you act?
secenekler: I should slow down, stop, and let the pedestrian cross because I have to give way
I should continue driving; the pedestrian is at the kerb and must give way to me
I should continue driving; since it is not a crossing, the pedestrian must give way to me
aciklama: According to the traffic sign, you are in a pedestrian zone. In pedestrian zones, drivers have an absolute obligation to give way to pedestrians. You must reduce speed to walking pace (approx. 7 km/h) and ensure pedestrians can pass safely.

soru: You are driving in city traffic and are about to pass a cycle crossing. A moped class II is approaching the cycle crossing from the right. What applies?
secenekler: The exit rule applies
The moped rider must give way to me
The right-hand rule applies
I must give way to the moped rider
aciklama: A cycle crossing is clearly marked with traffic signs and road markings. As a car driver, you have to give way to cyclists and moped class II at the cycle crossing. It is important to distinguish between a cycle crossing and a cycle passage.

soru: What does this traffic sign mean?
secenekler: Cycle crossing
Shared pedestrian and cycle path
Warning for cyclists
Cycle path
aciklama: This sign indicates a cycle crossing. Drivers have to give way to cyclists and moped class II at the crossing.

soru: Which vehicles are allowed on a cycle path?
secenekler: Only bicycles
Bicycles and moped class I
Bicycles and moped class II
Bicycles and moped class I and II
aciklama: On cycle paths, it is permitted for cyclists and moped class II to travel. Moped class I, which has a higher speed, is prohibited from using the cycle path.

soru: You are driving the green car. Do you have to give way to the cyclist?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: In case A, it is an uncontrolled cycle passage. There, cyclists have to give way to drivers. In case B, it is a cycle crossing, which is marked with signs and road markings, and there drivers have to give way to cyclists and moped class II.

soru: You are about to drive onto a cycle street. What applies?
secenekler: Vehicles on the cycle street must give way to me
I must give way to vehicles on the cycle street
It is mutual interaction between me and vehicles on the cycle street
aciklama: When entering a cycle street, you have to give way to vehicles already on the street. On cycle streets, the maximum speed is 30 km/h, you must adjust your speed to cycle traffic, and parking is only allowed in specially marked spaces.

soru: Which vehicles are allowed to go straight ahead?
secenekler: Line traffic and vehicles over 3.5 tonnes
Buses, motorcycles, and moped class I
Only bicycles
Line traffic, bicycles, and moped class II
aciklama: The blue round sign means 'Carriageway or lane for line traffic etc.'. According to this sign, it is permitted for line traffic (buses etc.), cyclists, and moped class II to go straight ahead.

soru: It is Saturday and the time is 7:00 AM. Is it allowed to use the lane indicated by the sign combination in the picture?
secenekler: Yes, because the lane is reserved for line traffic between 10:00 AM - 3:00 PM
No, because the lane is reserved for line traffic regardless of time
Yes, because the lane is reserved for line traffic between 4:00 PM - 7:00 PM
No, because the lane is reserved for line traffic between 6:00 AM - 9:00 AM
aciklama: The time indications on supplementary signs are read as follows: Black/white numbers without parentheses refer to weekdays (Monday-Friday), black/white numbers within parentheses refer to Saturdays, red numbers refer to Sundays and public holidays. Since it is Saturday at 7:00 AM, the time in parentheses applies (10-15). The lane is only reserved for buses/line traffic between 10:00 AM-3:00 PM on Saturdays, so at 7:00 AM it is allowed to drive in the lane.

soru: What applies when passing an uncontrolled cycle passage?
secenekler: I must adjust my speed so that road users at the passage are not exposed to danger
I have to give way to road users at the passage
I should apply the right-hand rule
aciklama: At uncontrolled cycle passages, cyclists crossing the road have to give way to drivers. But as a driver, you also have a duty to adjust your speed and drive safely to reduce the risk of collision with cyclists.

soru: You are driving in a roundabout. A vehicle is approaching from the right to enter the roundabout. What applies?
secenekler: I must stop and let the vehicle in
Neither I nor the other vehicle has to give way, it is mutual interaction
I have priority because I am already driving in the roundabout
According to the right-hand rule, I have to give way to that vehicle
aciklama: Vehicles already in the roundabout have priority. Vehicles approaching to enter the roundabout must give way to traffic in the roundabout.

soru: Must you signal when leaving a roundabout?
secenekler: Yes, with the right indicator
No, I only need to signal when entering the roundabout to show where I am going
Yes, with the left indicator
aciklama: When leaving a roundabout, you must always use the right indicator to show your intention and that you are about to leave the roundabout.

soru: You are approaching a roundabout and are going to turn left. Which lane should you position yourself in?
secenekler: Left lane
Right lane
aciklama: Unless otherwise indicated or road markings show, you should position yourself in the left lane when turning left in a roundabout. When going straight ahead or turning right, you should choose the right lane.

soru: What is the purpose of roundabouts?
secenekler: To make traffic more difficult to make drivers more experienced
To increase traffic flow and reduce the number of accidents
To make roads more varied to reduce the risk of drivers falling asleep at the wheel
aciklama: Roundabouts are designed to increase traffic flow and significantly reduce the risk of serious injuries and fatal accidents compared to traditional intersections.

soru: In a roundabout with lane guidance, you are going to turn left. What is correct?
secenekler: I can choose to drive in either the right or left lane
I must drive in the left lane
I must drive in the right lane
aciklama: Although the main rule for left turns in roundabouts is to choose the left lane, the lane guidance in this case shows that both the right and left lanes can be used for left turns. You can therefore choose either lane.

soru: Must you always stop before entering a roundabout?
secenekler: Yes, but vehicles in the roundabout must give way to me
Yes, and I must give way to vehicles in the roundabout
No, but I must give way to vehicles in the roundabout
aciklama: You do not need to stop completely before entering a roundabout unless there is a STOP sign. But you have to give way to traffic in the roundabout, so you can enter without stopping if the roundabout is empty or there is a safe gap.

soru: You are approaching a roundabout and want to turn around (make a U-turn). Can you use the roundabout to turn around?
secenekler: No, in a roundabout I must either go straight ahead or turn right/left
Yes, but it is not a recommended method
Yes, it is considered traffic-safe
aciklama: Using a roundabout to turn around is a recommended method. It is much safer than making a U-turn on narrow roads or performing risky manoeuvres.

soru: If you are going to turn right at an intersection, how should you position your car?
secenekler: As close to the right side as possible
Near the centre of the road
As close to the left side as possible
aciklama: When turning right at an intersection, you should position your car as close to the right side as possible both before and after the turn. This makes your intention clear to other drivers and reduces risk in traffic.

soru: You are going to turn left on a one-way street. How should you position your car?
secenekler: As close to the left side as possible
In the middle of the road
As close to the right side as possible
aciklama: On regular two-way roads, you should position yourself near the centre of the road when turning left. But on a one-way street, there is no oncoming traffic, so you should position your car as close to the left side as possible when turning left.

soru: If you are going to turn left at an intersection, how should you position your car?
secenekler: As close to the right side as possible
As close to the left side as possible
Near the centre of the road
aciklama: As a main rule, when turning left at an intersection, you should position your car near the centre of the road. The exception is one-way streets, where you should position yourself near the left side instead.

soru: You are in an acceleration lane. What should you do in this situation?
secenekler: I must stop before entering the motorway
I must give way to all traffic on the motorway
I should adjust my speed to merge into a safe gap without disturbing traffic
aciklama: When using the acceleration lane, there is mutual interaction with traffic on the motorway. You should not stop completely, but adjust your speed to motorway traffic and safely merge into a suitable gap.

soru: You are driving on a motorway-like road and see a person ahead wanting to hitchhike with their thumb out. Is it allowed to stop and pick up the hitchhiker?
secenekler: Yes, if it does not create any danger
No, it is not allowed to stop on motorway-like roads
Yes, it is allowed to stop but not to park
Yes, it is allowed on motorway-like roads but not on motorways
aciklama: On motorways and motorway-like roads, it is generally forbidden to stop or park. Stopping is only allowed at designated rest areas or parking spaces. You are therefore not allowed to stop to pick up a hitchhiker.

soru: What applies when you change lanes from the acceleration lane onto the motorway?
secenekler: It is mutual interaction and cooperation
All traffic on the motorway must give way to me
I must give way to all traffic on the motorway
aciklama: When merging onto the motorway, neither you in the acceleration lane nor the traffic on the motorway have direct right of way. It is mutual interaction. You in the acceleration lane should ensure a safe merge, while traffic on the motorway should facilitate by adjusting speed.

soru: A friend's car has broken down on the motorway and he asks you to come and tow him. Is this allowed?
secenekler: Yes, there is no specific rule, but it must be done without danger to others
Yes, but it must be done on the shoulder and only to the nearest suitable exit
Yes, but I may not drive faster than 20 km/h
No
aciklama: It is absolutely forbidden to tow vehicles on motorways and motorway-like roads. If a vehicle breaks down, a tow truck must be called. Only a vehicle that is already travelling on the motorway and stops may be towed on the shoulder to the nearest exit.

soru: You are driving on a motorway and approaching an on-ramp. What applies?
secenekler: I must always slow down
I should facilitate for merging vehicles to join
I must change to the left lane to avoid collision
I have to give way to merging vehicles
aciklama: When approaching an on-ramp, you should facilitate for merging vehicles to join. This is mutual interaction and cooperation; neither party has direct right of way, but you should adjust your speed to facilitate the merge.

soru: Which of the following is forbidden on motorways?
secenekler: Driving a light motorcycle
Driving with a trailer
Driving in reverse
Overtaking before a curve
aciklama: Reversing, U-turns, stopping, and parking are absolutely forbidden on motorways. There is no restriction on light motorcycles or vehicles with trailers driving on motorways, and due to one-way traffic and multiple lanes, overtaking before curves is allowed.

soru: Is it allowed to make a U-turn on a motorway-like road?
secenekler: No
Yes, U-turns are allowed but not manoeuvring turns
Yes, if I do not obstruct other traffic
aciklama: On motorway-like roads, the same rules apply as on motorways. It is not allowed to turn or reverse on these roads.

soru: Which vehicles are allowed to be driven on motorways?
secenekler: Light motorcycle, passenger car, and lorry
Bus, tractor, and lorry
Lorry, passenger car, and tractor
Passenger car, bus, and moped
aciklama: On motorways, only motor vehicles that can maintain a certain speed are allowed. Pedestrians, cyclists, mopeds, and tractors are prohibited on motorways. Therefore, light motorcycles, passenger cars, and lorries may use the motorway.

soru: What does speed blindness lead to?
secenekler: I feel that I am driving faster than I actually am
I feel that I am driving slower than I actually am
I feel that the car is moving even when it is stationary
aciklama: Speed blindness occurs when you have been driving at high speed for a long time and then slow down. It creates a feeling that you are driving slower than you actually are, which can lead to underestimating the braking distance and braking too late in dangerous situations.

soru: You are driving on a motorway with heavy traffic and have signalled to change lanes. What applies?
secenekler: Since I have signalled, I may change lanes immediately
Vehicles in the lane I am entering must give way to me
I must ensure that the lane change can be done safely
aciklama: Even if you have signalled, it is your responsibility to check that the lane change can be done safely without exposing other traffic to danger.

soru: Which statement about aquaplaning is correct?
secenekler: If the car is equipped with ABS, the risk of aquaplaning is less
High speed increases the risk of aquaplaning
The condition of the tyres does not affect the risk of aquaplaning
aciklama: The higher the speed, the more difficult it is for the tyres to disperse water underneath them, which increases the risk of aquaplaning. Worn tyres also directly increase the risk, while ABS does not prevent aquaplaning from occurring.

soru: What distance should you keep to the vehicle in front?
secenekler: At least three car lengths
At least 30 metres
At least six car lengths
Use the three-second rule to determine the distance
aciklama: The safe following distance depends on your speed. Therefore, the three-second rule is the most correct method instead of fixed metres or car lengths. Another rule of thumb is to keep a distance in metres corresponding to the speed in km/h.

soru: What is the most important reason for keeping sufficient distance to the vehicle in front?
secenekler: To reduce the risk of rear-ending the vehicle in front
To reduce the risk of colliding with wild animals
To reduce the risk of dazzling other drivers with high beams
aciklama: Many accidents are caused by drivers driving too close to the vehicle in front. Keeping sufficient following distance is crucial to be able to stop if the vehicle in front suddenly brakes, thereby minimising the risk of rear-end collisions.

soru: How is the braking distance affected if you double your speed?
secenekler: Doubled
Tripled
Quadrupled
Unchanged
aciklama: The braking distance increases quadratically with speed. When the speed doubles, the braking distance quadruples.

soru: It is dark and you are in a traffic queue. The car behind is uncomfortably close. What should you do?
secenekler: Increase the distance to the vehicle in front
Drive onto the shoulder, stop, and let the car behind overtake you
aciklama: By increasing the distance to the vehicle in front, you get more time to brake and avoid having to make a sudden stop. If you brake suddenly with a car close behind, you risk being rear-ended.

soru: You are driving at 110 km/h on a motorway and turn off onto an exit ramp. The speed limit on the ramp is 50 km/h. If you do not look at the speedometer, what are you likely to do?
secenekler: Reduce speed too little and drive faster than 50 km/h
Reduce speed to 70 km/h because the speed on exit ramps is only a recommendation
Reduce speed too much and drive slower than 50 km/h
aciklama: It is easy to suffer from speed blindness on the motorway. Speed blindness makes you feel that you are driving slower than you actually are. Therefore, if you do not look at the speedometer, you will likely not reduce your speed enough and thus exceed the limit.

soru: What is the first thing you should do when you are going to turn left on a country road?
secenekler: Signal
Reduce speed
Change down
Check traffic behind me
aciklama: Before starting a left turn, you must first check traffic behind you to see if you can safely perform the turn without risk of being rear-ended. If the turn is too risky, it is safer to continue straight ahead and turn around at a suitable place.

soru: You are driving on a country road and want to turn towards Köping. How should you position your car?
secenekler: As close to the right side as possible
Near the centre of the road
As close to the left side as possible
aciklama: According to the traffic sign, it is forbidden to turn directly left at the next intersection. To get to Köping, you must first turn onto the right slip road and then cross the road at a right angle. Since you are going to turn right, you should position the car as close to the right side as possible.

soru: You are going to turn left at an intersection. What is the most important thing to think about?
secenekler: Turn as quickly as possible to reduce the risk of accidents
Do not give priority to traffic from the left
Do not turn until I do not pose any danger to oncoming traffic or vehicles behind me
aciklama: Left turns on country roads are a very risky manoeuvre. Vehicles behind may come at high speed and there may be heavy oncoming traffic. You should only turn when you do not pose any danger to oncoming or following traffic. If the risk is too great, it is safer to continue driving and turn around at a suitable place.

soru: If you want to go towards Boda, what type of turn must you make?
secenekler: Safe left turn
U-turn
A regular left turn
Spanish turn
aciklama: The sign shows a 'Spanish turn'. In this type of intersection, it is forbidden to turn left directly. Instead, you turn onto the right slip road, which then curves back and crosses the main road at a right angle, enabling a safe passage across the road without the risky left turn.

soru: Which of the following traffic situations is generally most accident-prone?
secenekler: Right turn on a main road
Left turn on a main road
Right turn on a country road
Left turn on a country road
aciklama: Left turns on country roads are one of the most risky and complex manoeuvres in traffic. Misjudgements and high speeds often lead to serious accidents in these situations.

soru: You are driving the yellow car on a country road with a shoulder and good visibility. You are going to turn right and there is traffic behind you. How should you position your car?
secenekler: I should position myself in the middle of my lane
I should position myself far to the right on the shoulder
I should position myself far to the right in the lane
aciklama: When visibility is good, the shoulder can be used when turning right. You should then position yourself far out on the shoulder to facilitate traffic behind you passing and not to obstruct the flow.

soru: You are going to turn towards Katrainedal. What should you consider?
secenekler: That the road I am turning onto is a main road
That the road I am turning onto may only be used by residents
That the road I am turning onto may be in poor condition and lack traffic signs
aciklama: The orange direction sign shows that the road you are turning onto is a private road. Driving on private roads involves certain risks, as they may be poorly maintained and lack standardised traffic signs. There is no general restriction that they may only be used by residents.

soru: How should you behave when passing a horse rider?
secenekler: I should increase speed to shorten the overtaking time
I should flash my high beams to announce that I am passing
I should honk to announce that I am passing
I should reduce speed and drive calmly
aciklama: When driving near horses, you should always show consideration and avoid frightening the horse. You should therefore reduce speed, drive calmly, avoid sudden accelerations, avoid using sound or light signals, and keep a large lateral safety distance.

soru: What is the purpose of the so-called three-second rule?
secenekler: A method for determining where a meeting place should be
A method for estimating the minimum distance to the vehicle in front
A method for calculating the reaction distance
A method for calculating the stopping distance
aciklama: The three-second rule is a method for measuring the safe following distance to the vehicle in front by using a fixed point at the roadside. If you reach the same point earlier than three seconds after the vehicle in front passed, the distance is too short.

soru: You are driving on a country road with a dashed edge line. What should you use the shoulder for?
secenekler: I must always use the shoulder when someone wants to overtake me
I may only use the shoulder if necessary to avoid a dangerous situation
I can temporarily use the shoulder to facilitate other vehicles passing
aciklama: On roads with a dashed edge line, the shoulder can be used temporarily to facilitate following traffic overtaking or passing. It is not mandatory, however, and the shoulder is not only for dangerous situations.

soru: You are about to pass under a viaduct. The height is 4.2 metres. Must the viaduct be signposted?
secenekler: Yes, it must always be signposted
Yes, because it is under 4.5 metres
No, because it is over four metres
aciklama: Viaducts with a height under 4.5 metres must be signposted with traffic signs. If a viaduct lacks a height restriction sign, it means the height is at least 4.5 metres.

soru: What is a slow vehicle lane on an uphill grade?
secenekler: An area where overtaking is prohibited due to the uphill grade
A lane reserved for line traffic
An extra lane on hills to facilitate overtaking
aciklama: On long and steep hills, heavy trucks may have difficulty maintaining speed, which can disrupt traffic flow. To facilitate overtaking and improve traffic flow, there is sometimes an extra lane on the left side, which is called a slow vehicle lane on an uphill grade.

soru: You are approaching this traffic sign and see an oncoming vehicle further ahead. If there is not enough space to meet, who should stop at the meeting place?
secenekler: The driver who has the sign on the right
The driver who has the sign on the left
The driver who first arrived at the meeting place
aciklama: On narrow country roads, there are signposted meeting places where the road has been widened to facilitate meetings. If you see an oncoming vehicle and are at a meeting place, you should stop and wait there until the oncoming vehicle has passed. It is therefore the driver who first arrives at the meeting place who should stop.

soru: You are driving at 70 km/h. What is the minimum distance you should keep to the vehicle in front?
secenekler: 20 metres
35 metres
45 metres
70 metres
aciklama: In addition to the three-second rule, there is another rule of thumb for determining following distance: keep a distance in metres corresponding to your speed in km/h. If you are driving at 70 km/h, you should therefore keep at least 70 metres distance.

soru: You are on the shoulder and are about to drive back onto the carriageway. What applies?
secenekler: I should use the zipper principle
Traffic on the road has to give way to me
I have to give way to vehicles on the road
aciklama: The shoulder is only for temporary situations and not for long-term driving. When you are about to drive back onto the carriageway from the shoulder, you have to give way to all other vehicles on the road.

soru: Ahead of you, a vehicle with an LGF sign is driving. What is the maximum speed this vehicle may be driven at?
secenekler: 30 km/h
40 km/h
45 km/h
60 km/h
aciklama: To warn other road users, slow vehicles are equipped with a triangular LGF sign at the rear. The maximum permitted speed for vehicles with this sign is 45 km/h.

soru: You want to know the distance to the vehicle in front. Can you use the roadside posts to estimate the distance?
secenekler: No
Yes, because the distance between the posts is approximately 25 metres
Yes, because the distance between the posts is approximately 50 metres
Yes, because the distance between the posts is approximately 100 metres
aciklama: Reflective posts at the roadside can be used as a practical aid to estimate distance, as the distance between them on straight roads is approximately 50 metres. You can use this information or the three-second rule to measure your safe following distance.

soru: What should you primarily consider when adjusting speed at railway crossings?
secenekler: The speed limit on the road I am driving on
That I should not drive faster than 30 km/h when passing a railway crossing
How good visibility I have in both directions along the railway
aciklama: The most important factor determining what speed you should keep is how good visibility you have in both directions. If visibility is poor, it becomes more difficult to detect an approaching train, which requires a significantly lower speed.

soru: You are passing this traffic sign while driving. What should you do?
secenekler: I should reduce speed and be prepared to brake
I should always drive onto the shoulder to not disturb the workers
I should quickly pass to not disturb the workers
aciklama: When approaching a roadworks area, you must adjust your speed to the traffic situation. For your own and the road workers' safety, you should reduce speed and be prepared to stop or brake at any time.

soru: You are about to pass a railway crossing. The barriers are open and a white light signal is lit. Which statement is correct?
secenekler: Since the barriers are open, I can pass without risk
Despite barriers and signals, I must always check my surroundings
I must always stop before passing
aciklama: You should never blindly trust barriers and light signals. To eliminate the risk of technical failure, you should always check in both directions yourself to make sure no train is approaching before you pass.

soru: A train has just passed the railway crossing. Is it allowed to drive over the crossing now?
secenekler: No, because the signal shows red
Yes, because the barriers are open
Yes, if no other train is coming
Yes, if I drive at low speed and have a good safety margin
aciklama: As long as the red light is on at a railway crossing, it is absolutely forbidden to pass, regardless of whether the barriers are open or closed. You must wait until the red light goes out.

soru: You see a road maintenance vehicle driving on the left side of the road. Is the driver making a mistake?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: Road maintenance vehicles may need to drive on the left side of the road, for example during roadworks. These vehicles are therefore exempt from the usual rules about lane positioning.

soru: In both cases, you are about to pass a railway crossing and in both cases you see that no train is coming. Must you stop before passing?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: In case A, you must stop because there is a STOP sign. In case B, you do not need to stop. If the barriers are open, the signal shows white, and you see that no train is coming, you may pass without stopping.

soru: What should you do in this situation?
secenekler: Continue driving as usual, the red flag is just a warning
Reduce speed and pass the road worker slowly
Stop and wait until the road worker lowers the flag and then continue
aciklama: A road worker waving a red flag has the authority to stop traffic. You must therefore stop when a road worker shows a red flag, and wait until they lower the flag or give you permission to pass.

soru: You are driving towards a railway crossing with these traffic signs. At which sign should your speed be the lowest?
secenekler: A
B
C
aciklama: These signs show the distance to the railway crossing. The fewer stripes, the closer to the crossing. Alternative A with only one stripe shows the closest point to the crossing, and therefore your speed should be lowest there.

soru: You come to an unmanned railway crossing (without barriers and signals). Which is correct?
secenekler: I may overtake all vehicles
I may never overtake at a railway crossing
I may only overtake two-wheeled vehicles
aciklama: At unmanned railway crossings (without barriers and signals), there is a no-overtaking rule for all traffic except two-wheeled vehicles. If the crossing is manned (with barriers or signals), this prohibition does not apply.

soru: Is it allowed to overtake on a main road?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: There is no specific rule prohibiting overtaking on main roads. But as with all overtaking, it must be done safely without endangering traffic safety.

soru: You are driving at 70 km/h on a country road with a 70 km/h speed limit. The car behind wants to overtake you. Must you pull over?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: You are not obliged to pull over, but it is recommended if it facilitates the overtaking. Even if the overtaking is illegal and the overtaking vehicle is driving faster than the speed limit, you should facilitate the overtaking.

soru: You are driving behind a cyclist on a straight road. Is it allowed to overtake the cyclist when approaching an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing?
secenekler: No
Yes
aciklama: Immediately before uncontrolled pedestrian crossings, there is generally a no-overtaking rule, and this prohibition also applies to overtaking two-wheeled vehicles such as bicycles.

soru: You have started an overtaking of the vehicle in the picture but notice that a vehicle is approaching far away in the opposite direction. What should you do?
secenekler: Honk to warn oncoming traffic
Increase speed, overtake the vehicle, and then return to the right lane
Brake, abort the overtaking, and return to the right lane
Flash high beams to warn oncoming traffic
aciklama: An overtaking may only be done if there is no danger. Since there is oncoming traffic and a risk of a head-on collision, you must immediately brake, abort the overtaking, and return to the right lane.

soru: Is it allowed for moped and bicycle riders to overtake vehicles on the right side?
secenekler: Yes
No
Yes, but only in pedestrian zones
Yes, but only in traffic queues
aciklama: Moped and bicycle riders may pass vehicles on the right side. But if you are driving on a cycle path, the same positioning rules apply as on the road: you should keep to the right and overtake on the left side.

soru: You are driving on a single-lane country road and approaching a hill crest. Is it allowed to overtake immediately before the hill crest?
secenekler: No
Yes, if the vehicle in front signals that there is no oncoming traffic
Yes, but only if I make a quick overtaking with a speed advantage
aciklama: Overtaking is not allowed at hill crests or in curves where visibility is obscured. Exception: if there are multiple lanes in your direction of travel, or if you do not need to cross the centre line for the overtaking.

soru: You are considering overtaking the cyclist in the picture. How should you do it?
secenekler: Wait until the curve is over before overtaking
Honk to signal to the cyclist, who must then stop until I have passed
Keep extra distance to the cyclist during the overtaking
aciklama: Since you cannot see what is hidden behind the curve, it is very risky to overtake in this situation. There could be oncoming traffic or a pedestrian crossing, which would endanger traffic safety. You should therefore wait until the curve is over before overtaking.

soru: In which situation is it not allowed to overtake on a motorway?
secenekler: In the dark
Immediately before a sharp curve
Immediately before a hill crest
When a vehicle behind you has started an overtaking
aciklama: When another vehicle has started to overtake you, you may not increase your speed or start an overtaking yourself. On motorways with multiple lanes in the same direction, curves and hill crests are normally not an obstacle to overtaking, but you may not overtake when someone else is overtaking you.

soru: The red car in front of you is about to pass the grey car on the left on the right side. Is this allowed?
secenekler: No, overtaking on the right side is never allowed
Yes, the lanes lead to different destinations
aciklama: On roads with two or more lanes in the same direction, you should normally overtake on the left side. But if the lanes are divided with lane guidance signs leading to different destinations, it is allowed to pass vehicles on the right side.

soru: You are driving at 50 km/h on a road with a 70 km/h limit. You notice that the car behind starts to overtake you. What rules apply to you?
secenekler: I may increase my speed during the overtaking as long as I do not exceed 70 km/h
I may not increase my speed and should keep to the right to facilitate the overtaking
