aciklama: When a vehicle overtakes you, you may not increase your speed. To facilitate the overtaking, you should keep to the right (and use the shoulder if necessary) and in heavy traffic reduce your speed further to facilitate.

soru: Which type of overtaking is best for the environment?
secenekler: Accelerating overtaking
Flying overtaking
aciklama: A flying overtaking means you approach the vehicle in front at high speed and change lanes without slowing down. This method is better for the environment than an accelerating overtaking, because you do not need to accelerate extra to complete the passage.

soru: You meet a vehicle in the dark. When should you turn on high beams?
secenekler: Long before the meeting
When the vehicles are level with each other
After the meeting
aciklama: On a dark road without street lighting, you should have high beams on as much as possible for better visibility. You should turn on high beams only when you are level with the oncoming vehicle to avoid dazzling the driver. Turning them on before the meeting dazzles the oncoming driver.

soru: You are driving in the dark. Which lights should be on in the situation in the picture?
secenekler: Parking lights
Daytime running lights
Dipped headlights
High beams
aciklama: In the dark or with reduced visibility, it is mandatory to use dipped headlights. Parking lights are too weak for driving, and daytime running lights may only be used as an alternative to dipped headlights in good visibility. Since you are following a vehicle from the front, high beams would dazzle the driver in front, which would be wrong.

soru: What is the greatest risk when meeting other vehicles in the dark?
secenekler: Driving towards the light and colliding with the oncoming vehicle
Having difficulty identifying what type of vehicle is approaching
Visibility is reduced due to dazzling from the oncoming vehicle's lights
aciklama: To avoid dazzling, you should not stare at the oncoming vehicle's lights. If you are dazzled, you can temporarily become completely blind, meaning your visibility is reduced to zero metres.

soru: You are driving in the dark. In which situation can you wait the longest before turning off high beams (switching to dipped headlights) when meeting a vehicle?
secenekler: Case A
Case B
Case C
Case D
aciklama: In a left curve (Case D), you can keep high beams on longer when meeting a vehicle. Since high beams shine straight ahead in a straight line, which in a left curve directs the light towards the right side of the road, it will not dazzle the oncoming driver as early.

soru: You are driving in the dark on a street with street lighting as shown in the picture. Which lighting should you use?
secenekler: Dipped headlights
High beams
Parking lights
Fog lights
aciklama: In the dark, you should normally use high beams as often as possible. But if the road has sufficient and satisfactory street lighting, it is mandatory to use dipped headlights instead of high beams.

soru: You are driving in the dark with dipped headlights and approaching a pedestrian who has no reflector and is wearing dark clothes. At approximately what distance do you spot the pedestrian?
secenekler: Approximately 100 metres
Approximately 75 metres
Approximately 50 metres
Approximately 25 metres
aciklama: In the dark with dipped headlights, a pedestrian without a reflector and with dark clothes can be spotted at only about 25 metres distance. If the pedestrian had a reflector, this distance would increase to 125 metres. Therefore, reflectors are vital in the dark.

soru: In which situation is it allowed to use high beams?
secenekler: When meeting another car
When meeting a pedestrian
When meeting a moped
When meeting a tram
aciklama: It is forbidden to use high beams when meeting other vehicles, trams, trains, or ships due to the risk of dazzling. But when meeting a pedestrian, you should keep high beams on. This allows you to see the pedestrian better, and pedestrians' eyes are not as easily dazzled as car drivers'.

soru: You are driving in the dark on a country road and approaching a hill crest. A lorry is coming from the other side. When should you turn off high beams?
secenekler: When I see the lorry's roof lights
When I am level with the lorry
When I see the lorry's headlights
aciklama: Lorry drivers sit higher up and are therefore dazzled earlier than car drivers at hill crests. You should therefore immediately turn off high beams as soon as you see the roof lights of the oncoming lorry.

soru: You are driving in the dark with dipped headlights. At what distance do you spot a pedestrian with a reflector under normal conditions?
secenekler: Approximately 40 metres
Approximately 90 metres
Approximately 125 metres
Approximately 150 metres
aciklama: In the dark with dipped headlights, a pedestrian with a reflector can be spotted at about 125 metres distance. Without a reflector and with dark clothes, this distance drops to 20-30 metres. With high beams, the detection distance for a reflecting pedestrian increases to 400-450 metres.

soru: How much greater is the accident risk when driving in the dark compared to daylight?
secenekler: The accident risk is two to three times greater in the dark
The accident risk is four to five times greater in the dark
The accident risk is the same in the dark as in daylight
aciklama: The accident risk when driving in the dark is two to three times higher than in daylight. About one third of all accidents with personal injuries occur in the dark.

soru: You are driving on a hot and sunny day and it suddenly starts to rain. When is the road grip at its worst?
secenekler: It doesn't matter how long it has been raining
When it has been raining for a while
When the rain has just started
aciklama: After a long hot and dry period, the risk of skidding is greatest when the rain has just started. The water dissolves dust, dirt, and oil residues on the road and creates an extremely slippery surface. After a period of rain, the slippery surface is washed away.

soru: You are trying to get your car started on a slippery road but cannot get going. What should you do?
secenekler: I start in second gear
I accelerate with the handbrake pulled and then release it
I accelerate more
aciklama: On slippery roads, too much acceleration in first gear can make the wheels spin freely. By starting in second gear, you reduce the power to the wheels, which helps maintain grip and facilitates starting.

soru: Risk of poor road grip also exists on hot summer days. When is this risk highest?
secenekler: On a five-year-old asphalt road
On a newly asphalted road
On a heavily packed gravel road
aciklama: During very hot summer days, a newly asphalted road can become so hot that tar seeps up to the surface, making the road extremely slippery.

soru: What is the greatest advantage of your car being equipped with ABS brakes?
secenekler: Even during panic braking, the car can still be steered
ABS brakes work worse in cold conditions
The braking distance is always shorter when braking
aciklama: The main purpose of ABS brakes is to prevent the wheels from locking during hard braking. This means the car does not skid and the driver retains steering control even during panic braking. ABS can lengthen the braking distance on gravel, snow, and ice, so the perception that it always shortens the distance is incorrect.

soru: Where is the risk of slippery conditions greatest?
secenekler: On a poorly maintained gravel road
On an old asphalt road
On a road with large amounts of wet leaves
On an asphalt road after heavy rain
aciklama: Especially during autumn, wet leaves on the road surface can significantly reduce tyre grip and create a slippery surface similar to ice. Therefore, be extra careful on roads with wet leaves.

soru: You are driving in winter and there is snow on the roads. Where is the risk of skidding greatest?
secenekler: On a straight asphalt road
On a slight hill
On a straight gravel road
At intersections
aciklama: When the road surface is covered with snow, the risk of skidding increases significantly in places where many vehicles stop and start, such as at intersections. The tyres' repeated standing and acceleration polish the snow and make the surface much more slippery.

soru: When the temperature is around zero degrees, where is the risk of hidden ice formation and slippery conditions greatest?
secenekler: On bridges and viaducts
On a heavily packed gravel road
In gentle curves
At hill crests
aciklama: Bridges and viaducts cool down much faster than regular roads because they are exposed to cold air both from below and above. Especially bridges over water have high humidity, which greatly increases the risk of hidden ice formation when the temperature is around zero degrees.

soru: How can you best reduce the risk of aquaplaning?
secenekler: By using tyres with at least 3.0 mm tread depth and driving at low speed
By using tyres with at least 3.0 mm tread depth and driving at high speed
By using tyres with at least 1.6 mm tread depth and driving at high speed
By using tyres with at least 1.6 mm tread depth and driving at low speed
aciklama: The tyre tread is designed to disperse water. As tyres wear, the tread depth decreases, increasing the risk of aquaplaning. High speed also makes water dispersal more difficult. The combination of at least 3.0 mm tread depth and low speed is therefore most effective for safety.

soru: If you have caused a traffic accident but your car has not been damaged, what are you obliged to do?
secenekler: I must inform all other parties involved about the accident
I must contact my insurance company and tell them about the accident
Since my car is not damaged, I have no obligations
aciklama: It is illegal to flee from a traffic accident. You must always leave your details to the other parties involved.

soru: If you accidentally hit a traffic sign, what is the first thing you should do?
secenekler: Contact my insurance company
Nothing special, traffic signs are checked and repaired regularly
Contact the police
Restore the traffic sign (straighten it)
aciklama: If you have accidentally damaged a road device, the first thing you should do is restore the traffic sign. If it is not possible to restore it, you should mark the location and contact the police.

soru: If you crash into and damage another car in a parking lot, what should you do?
secenekler: I should always report the damage to my insurance company
I should always report the damage to the Swedish Transport Administration
I should contact the nearest parking attendant
If I cannot reach the car owner, I should report the damage to the police
aciklama: If you do not take any action, this could be considered hit-and-run, which is a crime. Try to reach the car owner; if you cannot, contact the police.

soru: A motorcyclist overtaking you skids and collides with an oncoming vehicle. Do you have any obligations?
secenekler: Yes, I must stop at the scene, help the injured, and contribute to investigating the accident
Yes, I must stop at the scene, but only if my car has been damaged
No, I did not cause the accident
aciklama: If you are in any way involved in a traffic accident, you are obliged to contribute to the investigation, provide your details, and help injured persons. This rule applies regardless of whether you caused the accident or not.

soru: When is it illegal to move a vehicle that has been left standing due to a traffic accident?
secenekler: If multiple vehicles are involved in the accident
If a person involved has been driving under the influence of alcohol
If someone has been seriously injured or killed
If someone has been slightly injured
aciklama: In traffic accidents, vehicles that pose an obstacle or danger to other road users should be moved as soon as possible. If someone has been seriously injured or killed, vehicles may only be moved if they pose an immediate danger to other traffic.

soru: How can you best help a person who has been injured in an accident and is bleeding heavily from the leg?
secenekler: I apply a pressure bandage to the wound and then raise the leg
I give the person something to drink
I wait without doing anything until medical personnel arrive
aciklama: In cases of severe bleeding, you should try to keep the injured body part as elevated as possible. To stop the bleeding, apply a pressure bandage to the wound. If you do not have a pressure bandage, you can use two ordinary pieces of fabric, one placed directly on the wound and the other wrapped around it.

soru: Vision Zero is a traffic safety strategy in Sweden. What are its long-term goals?
secenekler: That the number of traffic accidents decreases by 5% each year
That no one should break traffic rules
That no one should be killed or seriously injured in traffic
That there should be no traffic accidents at all
aciklama: The Swedish Transport Administration's long-term goal in Sweden is that no one should be killed or seriously injured in traffic. This is called Vision Zero.

soru: If you are first at the scene of a traffic accident, what is the first thing you should do?
secenekler: Call 112
Warn other road users
Make an overall assessment of the situation
Collect information from those involved
aciklama: The first thing you should do is make an overall assessment of the situation to determine what needs to be done. Are there injured people who need help? Do police or ambulance need to be called? Do the involved vehicles pose a danger or obstacle, and do other road users need to be warned?

soru: How can you best help a person who has suffered circulatory failure (shock)?
secenekler: Give the injured person something to drink
Try to lay the injured person down and keep them warm
Wait until medical personnel can help the injured person
aciklama: You should do what you can to help the injured person until medical personnel arrive. In cases of circulatory failure, you should also open the airways and stop any bleeding. Important: Never give a person in circulatory failure anything to drink!

soru: You arrive at a traffic accident where two cars have collided head-on. You discover that a person is unconscious and has stopped breathing. What do you do?
secenekler: I lay the person on their back, raise their legs, and call for an ambulance
I ensure the airways are open, perform CPR, and call for an ambulance
I apply a pressure bandage around the chest, lay the person on their back, and call for an ambulance
Since I was not involved in the accident, I have no obligations
aciklama: Check the person's consciousness and breathing. If the person is unconscious, start by opening the airways by gently placing one hand on the forehead and two fingers under the chin, then tilt the head back. Check breathing by listening and watching for chest movement. If the person is breathing normally, place them in the recovery position. If the person is not breathing or breathing weakly/irregularly, call 112 and start CPR.

soru: What does the abbreviation LABC stand for?
secenekler: Larm, ambulance, bleeding, and chock
Life threat, ambulance, bleeding, and chock
Life threat, breathing, bleeding, and chock
aciklama: At an accident scene with injured persons, first aid may be needed – LABC stands for: Life threat, Breathing, Bleeding, and Chock (shock).

soru: You are driving on a road with a 90 km/h limit and suddenly have engine failure. Where should the warning triangle be placed?
secenekler: Approximately 15 metres in front of the car
Behind the car, at a distance that gives other drivers time to be warned
Next to the car
Approximately 15 metres behind the car
aciklama: If you are forced to stop in a dangerous place, you should set up a warning triangle on roads with a speed limit over 50 km/h. The triangle should be placed behind the car, at a distance of approximately 50–100 metres, so that other drivers have time to spot it.

soru: During which times of the day do most wildlife accidents occur?
secenekler: In the middle of the night
In the middle of the day
At dawn and dusk
aciklama: Animals are most active at dawn and dusk when they search for food and water, which makes the risk of wildlife accidents highest during these times.

soru: If you collide with a ______ you must report the accident to the police.
secenekler: Wolf
Fox
Badger
Rabbit
aciklama: In the event of a collision with certain larger or specific animals, you are obliged to report the accident to the police. These animals are: moose, roe deer, deer, bear, wolf, lynx, badger, otter, mouflon, wild boar, and eagle.

soru: Your car has had engine failure and you have been forced to stop in a place where stopping is prohibited. What applies then?
secenekler: If the road's speed limit is 60 km/h or higher, I must have the car towed as soon as possible
If the road's speed limit is 50 km/h or lower, I must have the car towed as soon as possible
Regardless of the speed limit, I must get the car away from the place as soon as possible
aciklama: If you have been forced to stop in a prohibited place, you must get the car away from the place as soon as possible, regardless of the road's speed limit. Whether you need to set up a warning triangle, however, depends on the speed limit.

soru: In which situation is the risk of wildlife accidents greatest?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Alternative A is correct because the forest is very close to the road, which increases the risk of not spotting wild animals running onto the road in time. Alternative B: incorrect, because a wildlife fence prevents animals from crossing the road. Alternative C: incorrect, because visibility is better and you can more easily see if animals are about to cross. Alternative D: incorrect, for the same reason as C.

soru: What is the first thing you should do if you collide with large wildlife?
secenekler: Contact the Swedish Transport Administration and wait
Contact the police and wait
Contact the Swedish Transport Agency and wait
Warn other road users
aciklama: First and foremost, you must warn other road users. If you have collided with moose, roe deer, wild boar, bear, deer, lynx, reindeer, red deer, otter, wolf, eagle, badger, or mouflon, you must also mark the location and report the accident to the police.

soru: What is the maximum total weight of a light trailer that you are always allowed to tow with a B driving licence?
secenekler: Max 950 kg total weight
Max 850 kg total weight
Max 750 kg total weight
Max 650 kg total weight
aciklama: With a B driving licence, you may tow a light trailer. A light trailer has a total weight of at most 750 kg. If the trailer weighs more than 750 kg, the combined total weight of the car and trailer must not exceed 3500 kg.

soru: A friend's car has broken down on the motorway and he asks you to come and tow him. Is this allowed?
secenekler: Yes, there is no specific rule, but it must be done without danger to others
Yes, but I may not drive faster than 20 km/h
Yes, but it must be done on the shoulder and only to the nearest suitable exit
No
aciklama: It is absolutely forbidden to tow vehicles on motorways and motorway-like roads.

soru: If the caravan you attach to your car is wider than the car, what must you do?
secenekler: I must mark the sides of the caravan's rear section with reflectors to warn others
I don't need to do anything, the caravan is already equipped with everything required
I must have extra rear-view mirrors to be able to see past the caravan
I must mark the caravan with an LGF sign (slow-moving vehicle)
aciklama: If you attach a trailer (e.g. a caravan) that is wider than the car, you must install extra rear-view mirrors on the car.

soru: Is it allowed to attach a trailer with studded tyres to a car that does not have studded tyres?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: If your car has studded tyres, the trailer must also have studded tyres. But if your car does not have studded tyres, it is allowed to attach a trailer with studded tyres.

soru: When attaching a trailer to the car, the safety cable must be correctly connected. Why is this so important?
secenekler: The safety cable reduces the risk of the trailer skidding
Without the safety cable, the trailer's regular brakes do not work
If the trailer comes loose from the car, the brakes are activated automatically via the safety cable
aciklama: The safety cable is connected to the car. If the trailer were to come loose, the cable is tensioned and activates the trailer's brakes.

soru: What is the most common braking system on trailers?
secenekler: Overrun brake (push brake)
Hydraulic brake
Pneumatic brake
aciklama: If the trailer's total weight exceeds 750 kg, it must be equipped with a service brake. The most common system is called an 'overrun brake'. When the car brakes, the drawbar on the trailer is pushed in towards the car's towbar and the trailer is braked automatically.

soru: Is the trailer counted as a light trailer in any of these cases?
secenekler: Yes, only in case A
Yes, only in case B
Yes, in both case A and B
No
aciklama: With a B driving licence, you may tow a light trailer. A light trailer has a total weight of at most 750 kg. If the trailer weighs more than 750 kg, the combined total weight of the car and trailer must not exceed 3500 kg. Case A: The trailer's total weight is under 750 kg (710 kg) and is therefore a light trailer. Case B: Combined total weight (810 kg + 2200 kg = 3010 kg) is under 3500 kg, so the trailer is counted as light in this case.

soru: Must all trailers be equipped with a parking brake?
secenekler: Yes
No, only trailers with a kerb weight over 400 kg
No, only trailers with a kerb weight over 750 kg
No, it is only a recommendation
aciklama: If the trailer's kerb weight exceeds 400 kg, it must be equipped with a parking brake.

soru: What can be the consequence of loading the trailer too heavily at the front, resulting in a high nose weight?
secenekler: If my car is rear-wheel drive, traction is reduced
The trailer's brakes get less braking effect
The dipped headlights dazzle oncoming traffic
The safety cable risks losing its function
aciklama: If the trailer is too front-heavy, a high nose weight occurs. This leads to the car's rear section sinking, the front being lifted, and the dipped headlights dazzling oncoming traffic. Steering ability is impaired, and on front-wheel drive cars, traction is reduced.

soru: What is the maximum permitted speed for a passenger car with a braked trailer on a motorway?
secenekler: 70 km/h
80 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
aciklama: For passenger cars with a braked trailer (or light trailer that meets certain conditions), the maximum permitted speed is 80 km/h, regardless of whether it is on a motorway or other road.

soru: When towing, how long can the tow rope be without needing to be marked?
secenekler: Two metres
Four metres
Six metres
Eight metres
aciklama: If the tow rope is longer than 2 metres, it must be clearly marked so that other drivers can spot it.

soru: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing with a rope?
secenekler: 30 km/h
40 km/h
50 km/h
70 km/h
aciklama: When towing with a rope, the maximum permitted speed is 30 km/h.

soru: What affects the nose weight when you have attached a trailer to your car?
secenekler: Where I place the load on the trailer
Only what type of trailer I have
The trailer's tyre pressure
aciklama: If the load is placed at the back of the trailer, the nose weight decreases, and if it is placed at the front, it increases. For good driving, the load should be evenly distributed.

soru: You are going to tow another vehicle. Which is correct?
secenekler: If the towed vehicle's brakes do not work, it is forbidden to drive faster than 20 km/h
It is allowed to tow long distances on the motorway
It is forbidden to tow a two-wheeled motorcycle
aciklama: It is forbidden to tow a motorcycle or for a motorcycle to tow another vehicle. Vehicles with faulty brakes may not be towed, but must be transported by a recovery vehicle. Towing is not allowed on motorways.

soru: If you load the trailer too heavily at the back and the nose weight becomes too low, what can this lead to?
secenekler: The dipped headlights dazzle oncoming traffic
The trailer's rear lights risk dazzling oncoming traffic
The trailer becomes unstable and may start to skid
Steering ability is impaired
aciklama: If the trailer is too rear-heavy, the nose weight becomes too low, which makes the trailer unstable and may cause it to start skidding.

soru: You reduce your speed from 100 km/h to 50 km/h. How does the braking distance change?
secenekler: It decreases to one quarter
It does not change
It becomes half as long
aciklama: The braking distance changes quadratically. If the speed doubles, the braking distance quadruples. If the speed halves, the braking distance decreases to one quarter.

soru: Which statement about the stopping distance is correct?
secenekler: The stopping distance is the distance the vehicle travels from when I detect the danger until I start braking
The stopping distance is the sum of the reaction distance and the braking distance
The stopping distance is the distance the vehicle travels from when I start braking until it stops
aciklama: The stopping distance is the distance the vehicle travels from when you detect the danger until it stops completely. The stopping distance consists of the reaction distance and the braking distance. Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance.

soru: What is the reaction distance?
secenekler: The time it takes for me to react
The distance the vehicle travels from when I detect the danger until I react
The distance the vehicle travels from when I start braking until it stops
aciklama: The reaction distance is the distance the vehicle travels from when you detect the danger until you start braking.

soru: You are driving at 20 km/h on dry asphalt. The braking distance is then 2 metres. How long will the braking distance be at 60 km/h on the same road?
secenekler: Approximately 4 metres
Approximately 6 metres
Approximately 12 metres
Approximately 18 metres
aciklama: The braking distance increases quadratically. If the speed doubles, the braking distance quadruples. If the speed triples, the braking distance increases ninefold. Therefore, the correct answer is 18 metres (2 * 9 = 18).

soru: You are driving at 100 km/h on a motorway-like road. Your reaction time is one second. How long is your reaction distance?
secenekler: Approximately 30 metres
Approximately 50 metres
Approximately 70 metres
Approximately 100 metres
aciklama: A simplified method for calculating the reaction distance: remove the last digit from the speed, multiply by 3, and then multiply by the reaction time (in this case 1 second). 100 km/h -> 10. 10 x 3 x 1 = 30 metres.

soru: What affects your reaction time?
secenekler: My speed
The car's braking system
My personal condition
The condition of the tyres
aciklama: Reaction time is not affected by external factors such as tyres, brakes, or speed. It is affected by driver-related factors such as fatigue, attention, experience, and similar.

soru: Which of the following does not affect the braking distance?
secenekler: The road's gradient
The car's weight
The condition of the tyres
The driver's reaction time
aciklama: The driver's reaction time affects the reaction distance, not the braking distance. However, the reaction time does affect the stopping distance because stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance.

soru: Which factors affect the length of the reaction distance?
secenekler: The vehicle's speed and road surface
The driver's reaction time and the vehicle's speed
The vehicle's speed and weight
The driver's reaction time and the vehicle's weight
aciklama: The reaction distance is the distance the vehicle travels from when you detect the danger until you start braking or avoiding the obstacle. Both your reaction time and the vehicle's speed affect it.

soru: When you need to brake in a dangerous situation, how can you prepare so that your reaction time is as short as possible?
secenekler: By keeping your foot ready over the brake pedal
By focusing your gaze on the vehicle in front
By always being mentally prepared to act
aciklama: Being mentally prepared is good, but the shortest reaction time is achieved by keeping your foot ready over the brake pedal. To be ready to brake, you must lift your foot from the accelerator and hold it over the brake pedal.

soru: You are driving and a roe deer suddenly runs out onto the road. In such unexpected situations, your normal reaction time is approximately?
secenekler: Approximately 0.2 seconds
Approximately 0.5 seconds
Approximately 1 second
Approximately 2 seconds
aciklama: A driver's normal reaction time is approximately 1 second. The reaction time is affected by the driver's general condition and is impaired by factors such as fatigue and alcohol.

soru: When speed increases, the reaction distance also increases. Which statement is correct?
secenekler: Three times higher speed gives three times longer reaction distance
Three times higher speed gives six times longer reaction distance
Three times higher speed gives nine times longer reaction distance
aciklama: The reaction distance increases proportionally. Three times higher speed therefore gives three times longer reaction distance. Six times higher speed gives six times longer reaction distance.

soru: You are driving at 50 km/h. You reach for a water bottle and lose focus on the road for three seconds. How far does the car travel during that time?
secenekler: Approximately 20 metres
Approximately 30 metres
Approximately 40 metres
Approximately 60 metres
aciklama: Simplified method: Remove the last digit from the speed, multiply by 3, and then multiply by the time (three seconds). 50 km/h -> 5. 5 x 3 x 3 = 45 metres (approximately 40 metres). Exact calculation: convert km/h to m/s by dividing by 3.6 and multiply by the time. 50 / 3.6 = 14 m/s. 14 x 3 = 42 metres (approximately 40 metres).

soru: You are driving at 70 km/h on a country road and see a roe deer run out onto the road 20 metres ahead. If the roe deer does not get out of the way, at what speed will you collide with it?
secenekler: Approximately 10 km/h
Approximately 30 km/h
Approximately 50 km/h
Approximately 70 km/h
aciklama: In this case, you must first calculate the reaction distance, i.e. the distance the car travels from when you detect the danger until you start braking. The reaction distance is estimated by removing the last digit from the speed and multiplying by 3: 70 km/h -> 7 x 3 = 21 metres. The roe deer is 20 metres ahead of you, and even your reaction and starting to brake take approximately 21 metres. Therefore, you will collide with the roe deer at the speed you are driving, i.e. 70 km/h. This estimate is based on a general reaction time of one second.

soru: Your car is fully loaded and you feel that the car turns less than you steer. Can you do anything about this?
secenekler: No, the problem can only be fixed by an authorised workshop
Yes, by distributing the load so that it is lighter at the front
Yes, by changing to rear wheels with better grip
Yes, by disengaging the clutch in curves
aciklama: More information about understeer and load distribution can be found in the car's instruction manual.

soru: What does oversteer mean?
secenekler: The car turns more than the steering wheel is turned
The car turns less than the steering wheel is turned
aciklama: In oversteer, the car takes the curve sharper than the steering angle indicates, and the rear tends to skid outwards.

soru: Which of the following is correct?
secenekler: Most cars today are rear-wheel drive
All cars are front-wheel drive
Front-wheel drive cars tend to be understeered
Rear-wheel drive cars tend to be understeered
aciklama: Most cars today are front-wheel drive. Front-wheel drive cars tend to be understeered (skid with the front wheels) in curves, while rear-wheel drive cars tend to be oversteered (skid with the rear wheels) compared to front-wheel drive cars.

soru: In a curve, you feel that the car turns less than you steer. What could this be due to?
secenekler: That the car's front is too heavy
That the rear tyres are worn and have poor grip
That you accelerate too much in the curve with a rear-wheel drive car
That the car's rear is too heavy
aciklama: When the car turns less than the steering angle, it is called understeer. A front that is too heavy affects the front tyres' grip in the curve, causing the car not to turn enough and instead push straight ahead.

soru: What should you consider when driving a rear-wheel drive car?
secenekler: If I accelerate too much, the car tends to understeer
If I accelerate too much, the rear can skid
If I accelerate too much, the front can skid
If I brake too hard, the car tends to understeer
aciklama: Rear-wheel drive means the engine's power is transferred to the rear wheels. Rear-wheel drive cars tend to be oversteered (skid with the rear end) compared to front-wheel drive cars. On slippery surfaces, too much acceleration can cause the rear wheels to lose grip and the rear to skid.

soru: What is the lowest legal tread depth for summer tyres?
secenekler: 1 mm
1.6 mm
2 mm
3 mm
aciklama: The lowest legal tread depth for summer tyres is 1.6 mm. Winter tyres must have at least 3.0 mm tread depth.

soru: Where should you mount the tyres with the best grip?
secenekler: On the rear axle
It doesn't matter
On the front axle
aciklama: Tyres on the same axle should have the same tread depth. To prevent the car's rear from skidding, it is crucial that the rear tyres have the best grip. If you buy two new tyres, they should therefore be mounted on the rear axle.

soru: After a puncture, you have fitted the spare tyre (emergency wheel). The nearest workshop is about 40 km away. Which road should you choose first?
secenekler: Motorway-like road with shoulder
Motorway
Country road with shoulder
aciklama: The spare tyre has a speed restriction (usually max 80 km/h) indicated on the tyre. Motorways and motorway-like roads have higher speed limits, which can be dangerous for you and other road users. Therefore, choose a country road with a lower speed limit.

soru: On 4 May, there are winter road conditions. Is it allowed to drive with studded tyres?
secenekler: No, after 15 April studded tyres are never allowed
No, after 30 April studded tyres are never allowed
Yes, because winter road conditions prevail
aciklama: The studded tyre ban normally applies between 16 April and 30 September. But if winter road conditions (snow, ice, slippery conditions, or slush) prevail or are expected, studded tyres are allowed even during this period.

soru: Why should you check and tighten the wheel bolts after changing a wheel?
secenekler: To prevent protruding bolts from causing a puncture
To reduce the risk of uneven tyre wear
To reduce fuel consumption
To ensure that no wheel comes loose
aciklama: After changing a wheel, you must retighten the bolts to ensure that no wheel comes loose. This should be done after driving approximately 50–100 km with the new wheels.

soru: On 25 March, you are going to drive from Stockholm to Jönköping and the road conditions look as shown in the picture. Which tyres are allowed?
secenekler: Studded tyres with 2 mm tread depth
Friction tyres (non-studded winter tyres) with 4 mm tread depth
Summer tyres with 7 mm tread depth
aciklama: Between 1 December and 31 March, winter tyres are mandatory in winter road conditions. Winter tyres must have at least 3.0 mm tread depth. Friction tyres are non-studded winter tyres and 4 mm tread depth is above the legal level, making them allowed.

soru: In winter road conditions, friction tyres can be used instead of studded tyres. Which statement about friction tyres is correct?
secenekler: They significantly reduce fuel consumption compared to studded tyres
They significantly increase fuel consumption compared to studded tyres
They wear less on the roads than studded tyres
aciklama: Studded tyres do not have a major impact on fuel consumption. However, studded tyres wear on the road surface and cause dangerous particles in the air. Therefore, studded tyres are prohibited in certain areas.

soru: Is it allowed to drive with non-studded winter tyres in summer?
secenekler: Yes, but only temporarily for short journeys
Yes, but it can impair the car's driving characteristics
No, it is forbidden to use winter tyres in summer
aciklama: It is legal to drive with friction tyres (non-studded winter tyres) in summer, but it is not recommended because they are designed for winter road conditions. It can impair the car's grip and driving characteristics.

soru: What can incorrect wheel alignment (tracking) lead to?
secenekler: Engine wear
Uneven wear on the front tyres
Heavier steering
Damage to the power steering
aciklama: If the car pulls to one side on a straight road, it may be due to incorrect wheel alignment. This causes the edges of the front tyres to wear abnormally quickly. Visit a workshop to fix the problem.

soru: What is the advantage of friction tyres compared to summer tyres?
secenekler: Better grip in winter road conditions
Better steering ability
Lower fuel consumption
aciklama: In winter road conditions, winter tyres are necessary for good grip. Alternatives are friction tyres, studded tyres, or summer tyres with snow chains.

soru: Must you always use winter tyres when there are winter road conditions?
secenekler: No
Yes
aciklama: According to the law, you are only obliged to use winter tyres between 1 December and 31 March if winter road conditions prevail. For example, if there is snow or ice on 6 April, you are not obliged to have winter tyres.

soru: You press the brake pedal when the engine is off. Which of the following is correct?
secenekler: The pedal should slowly sink downwards
The pedal should feel hard/stiff
The pedal should be as easy to press as the accelerator pedal
aciklama: Alternative 1 is incorrect: if the pedal slowly sinks, there is likely a leak in the brake system. Alternative 2 is correct. Alternative 3 is incorrect: if the brake pedal is as easy as the accelerator, something is wrong with the system.

soru: Is it allowed to drive a car where the foot brake does not work but the handbrake works?
secenekler: No, the car must be towed
Yes, as long as the handbrake works
Yes, to the nearest workshop
aciklama: If the foot brake is out of order and there is no braking effect on any wheel, it is absolutely forbidden to drive the car. It must be towed.

soru: What should you consider when towing with the engine off?
secenekler: The lighting does not work
The steering can become heavy
Gear shifting can become difficult
The brakes do not work
aciklama: Power steering facilitates steering with the help of hydraulics and a pump driven by the engine. When the engine is off, steering becomes very heavy and difficult.

soru: You press the brake pedal and when you start the engine, the pedal sinks slightly. What does it mean?
secenekler: That the brake system is starting to wear
That the brake servo is working as it should
That brake fluid is leaking
aciklama: To check the brake servo, press the brake pedal a few times with the engine off and then hold the pedal down while starting the engine. If the servo works correctly, the pedal should sink slightly when the engine starts.

soru: Your car is equipped with ABS brakes. Which statement is correct?
secenekler: ABS brakes work worse in cold weather
The braking distance is always shorter
Even during panic braking, the car can still be steered
aciklama: ABS prevents the wheels from locking during braking, which reduces the risk of skidding and allows you to steer the car even during panic braking. ABS can lengthen the braking distance on gravel, snow, and ice, but provides better steering control.

soru: Which statement about dual brake circuits is correct?
secenekler: Dual brake circuits are uncommon in modern cars
If one circuit fails, the car retains braking effect on some wheels
Dual brake circuits consist of parking brake and service brake
If one circuit fails, braking effect is lost on all wheels
aciklama: Dual brake circuits are designed to prevent all wheels from losing braking effect at the same time. If one circuit breaks, only two wheels lose braking power, while the other two still brake.

soru: You have just washed the car and notice that the brakes feel uneven. How can you easily fix this?
secenekler: Wait about 10 minutes before driving
Brake a few times at low speed
Turn off and turn on the ABS system
aciklama: Moisture on the brakes impairs braking performance. Therefore, you should always test the brakes after a car wash. By braking a few times, the brakes warm up and the moisture disappears.

soru: How do you check the ABS system?
secenekler: I brake hard and feel if the pedal vibrates (pulses)
I never need to check the ABS system
I pull the handbrake while driving and see if the wheels lock
aciklama: If the ABS system is out of order, a warning light should illuminate on the instrument panel. But to be sure, you can test by braking hard in a safe place and feeling if the brake pedal vibrates.

soru: How do you notice that the ABS brakes have stopped working?
secenekler: I can check it by starting the car with the brake pedal pressed down
A warning light on the instrument panel illuminates
The brake pedal becomes heavier
aciklama: If the ABS warning light illuminates on the instrument panel, you should visit a workshop to have the system repaired.

soru: How do you check if the power steering is working?
secenekler: I check if the steering wheel is heavy to turn with the engine off
I turn the steering wheel slightly while starting the engine
I never need to check it, a warning light illuminates in case of error
aciklama: With the engine off, the steering wheel should be heavy to turn. If the servo works correctly, the steering wheel should become easy to turn immediately when the engine starts.

soru: What happens if the brake servo stops working?
secenekler: The brakes stop working completely
It becomes heavier to brake, the pedal must be pressed harder
The wheels lock when braking
The ABS system stops working
aciklama: The brake servo amplifies your braking force. If the servo stops working, you can still brake, but the pedal becomes much heavier and requires more force.

soru: Which factor primarily determines what type of child car seat should be used?
secenekler: The child's age
It is up to the driver to decide
The child's height
aciklama: What type of protective device should be used is often indicated with age and/or weight, but the determining factor is the child's height.

soru: Which statement about child car seats is correct?
secenekler: A child car seat may not be installed in a seat with an active airbag
A child car seat may only be installed by an authorised workshop
A child car seat may only be installed in the back seat
aciklama: If a child car seat is placed on a seat with an airbag (the front seat), the airbag must be deactivated or disconnected.

soru: Which statement about airbags is correct?
secenekler: You should not sit closer than 25 cm from the airbag
Children are best protected in a child car seat in a seat with an airbag
The airbag should not be used together with a seat belt
The airbag always deploys in collisions
aciklama: The airbag should be used together with a seat belt. Since it deploys with great force, it can cause injuries if used without a belt or if you sit too close. Keep at least 25 cm distance from the steering wheel.

soru: To reduce the risk of injury from the airbag, it is recommended that you do not sit too close. What is the minimum distance between the body and the steering wheel?
secenekler: 25 cm
30 cm
45 cm
60 cm
aciklama: The recommended safe distance between the driver's body and the steering wheel is at least 25 cm to avoid injury when the airbag deploys.

soru: How tall must a child be to be able to use a regular seat belt?
secenekler: 110 cm
120 cm
135 cm
145 cm
aciklama: Children taller than 135 cm may use a regular seat belt. Shorter children must use a special protective device.

soru: Which statement about seat belts in passenger cars is correct?
secenekler: Seat belts should be used even in parking lots
It is the driver's responsibility that passengers under 15 use a seat belt
A small child sitting on an adult's lap can share the same belt
aciklama: The driver is responsible for passengers under 15 using a seat belt. In parking lots or petrol stations (at low speed), there is no seat belt requirement. A seat belt may never be used by two people at the same time.

soru: You are going to drive a two-year-old child to preschool but do not have a child car seat. How may you transport the child?
secenekler: Only in a taxi, if the journey is short and the child sits in the back seat
In your own car, if the journey is short and the child sits in the back seat
In your own car, if the journey is short and the child sits in the front seat
aciklama: If the child is over 3 years old and shorter than 135 cm, they may ride without a child car seat in the back seat on short journeys in your own car. But if the child is under 3 years old, it is only allowed in a taxi and then in the back seat.

soru: What obligation do you have as a driver regarding seat belts?
secenekler: I am obliged to ensure that everyone in the car uses a seat belt
I am obliged to ensure that all children under 15 use a seat belt or protective device
I am obliged to always use a seat belt, even in a parking lot
aciklama: Passengers over 15 are themselves responsible for their seat belt. In parking lots, there is no seat belt requirement. The driver's legal obligation is that children under 15 use a seat belt or appropriate protective device.

soru: Which light illuminates when the battery is not being charged?
secenekler: Lamp 9
Lamp 6
Lamp 10
Lamp 2
aciklama: Lamp 9 is the battery symbol and illuminates when there is a fault with the charging system (the battery is not being charged).

soru: You notice that the car consumes significantly more fuel than normal. What could be a likely cause?
secenekler: Clogged oil filter
Clogged air filter
Clogged fuel filter
A fuse has blown
aciklama: A clogged air filter makes it harder for the engine to draw in air, leading to incomplete combustion and increased fuel consumption.

soru: When is the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning greatest?
secenekler: When driving in built-up areas with open windows
When driving in a traffic jam with the AC on
When driving at low speed with closed windows
When the engine is idling in a poorly ventilated garage
aciklama: Even with a catalytic converter, exhaust gases contain harmful amounts of carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide is odourless and colourless, making it difficult to detect. Never start the engine in a closed garage or similar space.

soru: Your car does not start (Car A) and you must use jump leads from another car (Car B). Which is correct?
secenekler: The positive terminals are connected and the negative from Car B is connected to Car A's body
The engine of Car B must be turned off
It doesn't matter how the batteries are connected, I can try again
The batteries may have different voltages
aciklama: Procedure for jump leads: 1. Connect the positive terminals with a cable. 2. Connect the negative terminal of the donor battery (Car B) to a metal part of Car A's body (earth). 3. Start the engine of Car B. 4. Start the engine of Car A.

soru: What percentage of harmful substances does the catalytic converter clean?
secenekler: Over 99 %
aciklama: The catalytic converter converts approximately 80–95 % of the harmful substances in the exhaust gases into carbon dioxide and water. This means that carbon dioxide emissions do not decrease, which can only be addressed by reducing fuel consumption.

soru: Why are there fuses in the electrical system?
secenekler: To strengthen and weaken the current as needed
So that all lamps get the correct voltage
To protect electrical wires from overheating and fire
To reduce electricity consumption
aciklama: Fuses protect the car's electronics and prevent fire in the event of a short circuit. If an electronic device stops working, all fuses should be checked. They are usually located under the instrument panel or in the engine compartment.

soru: What should you do if the oil warning light illuminates?
secenekler: Stop the car and turn off the engine immediately
Continue driving and top up the oil when you get home
Stop, turn off the engine and let it rest for at least 10 minutes, then continue
aciklama: If the oil pressure warning light illuminates while driving, you must immediately stop in a safe place and turn off the engine. Topping up the oil may solve the problem, but if it does not, the car must be checked at a workshop to avoid serious engine damage.

soru: What should you top up with if the coolant is empty?
secenekler: Glycol and water
Distilled water
Alcohol
aciklama: The cooling system requires little maintenance, but it is important to regularly check the fluid level. If needed, you should top up with a mixture of water and glycol, which prevents freezing and corrosion.

soru: Is it allowed for the load to protrude on the sides of the car?
secenekler: No
Yes, max 10 cm on each side
Yes, max 20 cm on each side
Yes, max 30 cm on each side
aciklama: According to load regulations, the total width of the load including the vehicle must not exceed 260 cm. The load may protrude at most 20 cm on each side of the vehicle.

soru: This is your vehicle's registration certificate. What is the car's kerb weight?
aciklama: Total weight = Kerb weight + Maximum load. Kerb weight = Total weight - Maximum load. 1700 kg - 300 kg = 1400 kg.

soru: Which of the following options is correct?
secenekler: Kerb weight + Gross weight = Total weight
Maximum load + Gross weight = Kerb weight
Kerb weight + Maximum load = Total weight
Total weight + Maximum load = Kerb weight
aciklama: The total weight is the sum of the vehicle's kerb weight, maximum number of passengers (excluding the driver), and maximum load capacity.

soru: This is your vehicle's registration certificate. You, as the driver, weigh 70 kg and you have loaded 130 kg of luggage in the car. What is the car's gross weight?
aciklama: Gross weight is the vehicle's weight at a specific time and depends on how much load you have. Gross weight = Kerb weight (1040 kg) + load (130 kg) = 1170 kg. The driver's weight is already included in the kerb weight and is not counted again.

soru: What is the maximum number of passenger seats allowed in a passenger car?
secenekler: Four
Six
Eight
No limit
aciklama: The number of passenger seats is stated in the registration certificate. However, a passenger car may not have more than eight passenger seats.

soru: You have load protruding both front and rear. With the load, the car's length must not exceed ______ metres.
aciklama: With the load included, the total length of the vehicle must not exceed 24 metres. This also applies with a trailer. Exception: under certain conditions, the total length can be 25.25 metres.

soru: Your car is 240 cm wide. Is it allowed to drive with a load protruding 15 cm on each side?
secenekler: Yes, the load protrudes less than 20 cm
Yes, the total width is under 280 cm
No, the total width exceeds 260 cm
No, the load protrudes more than 10 cm
aciklama: The load may protrude 20 cm on each side as long as the total width does not exceed 260 cm. In this case, the total width is 240 cm + 15 cm + 15 cm = 270 cm, which exceeds 260 cm.

soru: When should the load be marked?
secenekler: All load that protrudes in front of or behind the car
All load that protrudes in front of the car and is not clearly visible
No load needs to be marked, but it facilitates for others
All load that protrudes behind the car
aciklama: All load that protrudes in front of the car must be marked. Exception: if it is clearly visible to other road users and does not protrude more than one metre forward. All load that protrudes more than one metre behind the car must also be marked.

soru: You have a load that protrudes two metres forward and two metres backward. Must the load be marked in the dark?
secenekler: Yes, front and rear with white reflector and white light
Yes, front and rear with red reflector and red light
No, the load does not need to be marked
Yes, front with white reflector and white light, rear with red reflector and red light
aciklama: Load that protrudes in front of the car or more than one metre behind the car should, in daylight, be marked with red-yellow flags. In the dark, the rear part should be marked with red light and red reflectors, and the front part with white light and white reflectors.

soru: Which light illuminates in the event of an ABS system fault?
secenekler: Lamp 10
Lamp 6
Lamp 4
Lamp 8
aciklama: In the event of an ABS system fault, a warning light with the text 'ABS' illuminates on the instrument panel. In the picture, this corresponds to lamp 8.

soru: Which light illuminates when the fuel level is low?
secenekler: Lamp 3
Lamp 7
Lamp 9
Lamp 1
aciklama: When the fuel level is low or the tank has reached the reserve level, the petrol symbol illuminates on the instrument panel. In the picture, this corresponds to lamp 1.

soru: Which light illuminates when the engine temperature is too high?
secenekler: Lamp 6
Lamp 3
Lamp 10
Lamp 2
aciklama: When the coolant temperature becomes too high (engine overheating), a thermometer symbol submerged in liquid illuminates. In the picture, this corresponds to lamp 10.

soru: Which light illuminates when the rear fog light is switched on?
secenekler: Lamp 5
Lamp 8
Lamp 9
Lamp 2
aciklama: When the rear fog light is activated, a fog light symbol with wavy lines in front of a horizontal line illuminates. In the picture, this corresponds to lamp 2.

soru: What does it mean when this light illuminates?
secenekler: The battery is overheating
The battery is not being charged
aciklama: The red battery symbol indicates a fault in the charging system. When the light is on with the engine running, it means the battery is not being charged, which is often due to a fault with the alternator or V-belt.

soru: Which light illuminates in the event of an airbag system fault?
secenekler: Lamp 4
Lamp 6
Lamp 5
Lamp 2
aciklama: In the event of a fault in the airbag or seat belt tensioner system, a symbol with a person sitting with a ball in front of them (airbag) illuminates. In the picture, this corresponds to lamp 4.

soru: What does it mean when this light is on?
secenekler: That the high beams are switched on
That the rear fog light is switched on
That the parking lights are switched on
aciklama: The blue symbol with straight beams indicates that the high beams are on. Dipped headlights are often symbolised with green and downward-pointing beams, while high beams are blue and horizontal.

soru: Which fluid do you need to top up when this light illuminates?
secenekler: Coolant
Windscreen washer fluid
Engine oil
Battery fluid
aciklama: The yellow symbol depicts the windscreen with washer and water jets. When the light illuminates, it means the washer fluid is empty or low and must be topped up.

soru: What should you do if the oil pressure warning light illuminates?
secenekler: Continue driving and top up the oil when I get home
Stop, turn off the engine and let it rest for at least 10 minutes, then continue
Stop the car and turn off the engine immediately
aciklama: If the oil pressure warning light illuminates while driving, you must immediately stop in a safe place and turn off the engine. Topping up the oil may solve the problem, but if not, a workshop must fix the fault to avoid serious engine damage.

soru: Why should you change brake fluid regularly every few years?
secenekler: It is a legal requirement to change brake fluid every three years
Brake fluid absorbs moisture (water)
Brake fluid becomes thicker over time
aciklama: Brake fluid is hygroscopic, meaning it absorbs moisture from the air. As the water content increases, the boiling point decreases, which can cause the fluid to boil during hard braking and air to enter the system (brakes fail). Therefore, it must be changed regularly.

soru: You have caused an accident with another car. What does the traffic insurance cover?
secenekler: The goods in the damaged car
All damage to both my car and the other car
Damage to my car
Damage to the other car
aciklama: Traffic insurance covers damage you cause to other vehicles, people, or property. It does not cover damage to your own car. To cover your own damage, you need a voluntary insurance such as comprehensive or partial insurance.

soru: Which document must you have with you when driving your passenger car?
secenekler: Receipt that the car is traffic insured
Driving licence
Inspection certificate
Registration certificate
aciklama: When driving a car, you must always have your driving licence with you. The other documents are not mandatory to carry, although they can be good to have.

soru: What happens if you do not inspect your car on time?
secenekler: The car may be used until the Swedish Transport Agency sends a stop notice
The car is automatically de-registered when the inspection time expires
The car may be used until the police send a stop notice
The car may be used until the Swedish Transport Administration sends a stop notice
aciklama: If you do not inspect the car within the specified time, the car is automatically de-registered (traffic ban) from that day. The car may then not be used in traffic, except to be driven to an inspection.

soru: Must you have traffic insurance to use your car on a public road?
secenekler: If I have not been involved in any accident for 10 years, I do not need traffic insurance
No, it is only a recommendation so that you do not have to pay for damage in traffic
Yes, always
aciklama: According to the law, you must always have traffic insurance to drive your car on a public road, regardless of when you were last involved in an accident.

soru: You have caused an accident with another car. Which insurance covers the damage to your own car?
secenekler: Traffic insurance
Comprehensive / Vehicle damage insurance
Home insurance
Partial insurance
aciklama: If you yourself caused the accident, only the vehicle damage insurance (comprehensive) covers the damage to your own car. Full comprehensive includes both traffic insurance and this damage insurance.

soru: What is a flying inspection (road check)?
secenekler: When the workshop checks the car during service
When customs stops me on entry or exit to Sweden
When the insurance company checks that the car has traffic insurance
When a police officer stops me while driving to check the car
aciklama: A police officer or vehicle inspector can at any time stop you on the road to check the car's technical condition and traffic safety. These unannounced road checks are called flying inspections.

soru: What can you find in the registration certificate?
secenekler: When the car must be inspected
The car's total weight
When the traffic insurance expires
aciklama: The registration certificate shows the car's technical data and owner. The total weight is a technical detail found there. Inspection periods are regulated by law and the insurance validity period is obtained from your insurance company.

soru: You have bought a new car and started using it immediately. When should you inspect it for the first time?
secenekler: Within one year
Within 14 months
Within two years
Within three years
aciklama: When a car should be inspected is determined by the car's age counted from the first registration date. Passenger cars must be inspected for the first time within three years from the month they were put into traffic. The second inspection takes place within two years, thereafter every 14 months.

soru: You have bought a used car. Within what time must you report the change of ownership?
secenekler: Within seven days
Within 10 days
Within two weeks
Within one month
aciklama: Both seller and buyer must report the change of ownership to the Swedish Transport Agency no later than 10 days after the sale or transfer took place.

soru: When must you inspect the car for registration inspection?
secenekler: Every other year
If I change to a different engine type
Every year
If I sell the car
aciklama: If you make permanent changes to the car that mean the information in the registration certificate is no longer correct, you must inspect the car. Changing to a different engine type is an example of such a change.

soru: Your car is seven years old and was last inspected on 25 February 2020. When is the latest you must inspect it?
secenekler: 28 February 2021
30 April 2021
28 February 2022
28 February 2023
aciklama: Passenger cars older than five years must be inspected every 14 months. The time is counted from the month when the last inspection was done. From February 2020, count 14 months forward, which falls in April 2021. The inspection must be completed by the last day of that month, i.e. 30 April 2021.

soru: You have made a change to the car that requires a registration inspection. Within what time must this inspection be done?
secenekler: Within 1 week
Within 10 days
Within 1 month
Within 3 months
aciklama: After a permanent change that affects the registration certificate, you must inspect the car no later than one month after the change was made.

soru: What can surface learning (memorisation) of traffic information lead to?
secenekler: That I do not understand the traffic rules and why they exist in depth
That I do not forget the information as easily after driving licence training
That I remember the information long after driving licence training
aciklama: Surface learning means you memorise information without understanding the logic. When you only study to pass the test and do not understand the reasoning, you forget the information just as quickly after the test.

soru: What do you achieve through "deep learning" during driving licence training?
secenekler: To fully understand the traffic rules and the logic behind them, and to be able to apply them in different situations
To memorise test questions and forget them immediately after the test
To only know the rules superficially to pass the theory test
aciklama: Deep learning means you understand why the rules exist and what they mean for safety and traffic flow. This makes the knowledge lasting and helps you make the right decisions in complex traffic situations.

soru: What is a positive effect of overlearning?
secenekler: It makes me always drive slower
Driving (technical skills) becomes more automatic
It makes it easier for me to estimate the speed of oncoming vehicles
aciklama: Overlearning means you practise until a skill becomes automatic. When you have reached that level in driving training, actions such as clutch, gear shifting, and steering become automatic, so you can focus on planning your driving and spotting hazards in traffic.

soru: What can learning through imitation lead to?
secenekler: That I develop as a driver by learning from my mistakes
That my reaction time improves
That I risk imitating others' bad/incorrect behaviours
That I develop as a driver by often watching car films
aciklama: Learning through imitation means you observe and copy other road users' behaviours. Inexperienced drivers tend to assume that others are more experienced and therefore copy their incorrect, rule-breaking, or aggressive behaviours, which can be dangerous.

soru: What is meant by learning through imitation?
secenekler: That I learn from experiences from previous situations
That I learn by being aware of what happens around me while driving
That I learn by seeing what others do
aciklama: Learning through imitation means you see what others do and mimic their behaviour. Inexperienced drivers tend to assume that others are more experienced and therefore copy their behaviours.

soru: What can probability-based learning lead to?
secenekler: That I drive slowly at a cycle crossing where cyclists rarely appear, despite good visibility
That I drive fast at a cycle crossing where cyclists rarely appear, despite poor visibility
That I drive fast at a cycle crossing where cyclists often appear, despite poor visibility
aciklama: Probability-based learning means you assess risk based on previous experiences. Therefore, you may drive fast at a cycle crossing despite poor visibility, because cyclists rarely come. This is negative, because you should adjust your speed according to visibility, regardless of how rarely cyclists appear.

soru: What does overlearning (practising until it becomes reflexive) lead to?
secenekler: That I become worse at handling dangerous situations in traffic
That I do not forget important details because I have practised so much
That I remember the information longer, even if I drive infrequently
aciklama: Overlearning is important during driving training. It means you practise until the technical actions become automatic. When you can manoeuvre the car without thinking, you can instead focus on planning your driving and spotting hazards. Overlearning also helps you retain your skills even if you do not drive for a long time.

soru: What is meant by microsleep?
secenekler: Sleeping deeply
Sleeping lightly
Taking a quick break
Short and unconscious moments of sleep
aciklama: Fatigue can creep up on you and you can lose concentration for a fraction of a second without noticing it. This is called microsleep.

soru: Which of the following is a sign of fatigue?
secenekler: That I feel stressed
That I feel cold
That I feel hungry
That I feel sweaty
aciklama: Pay attention to symptoms of fatigue! If you notice that you are starting to get tired, you can for example stop and stretch your legs or sleep for a short while.

soru: Which statement about the combination of drugs and driving is correct?
secenekler: Drugs have a positive effect on my driving
Only the sense of balance is affected by drugs
It is not illegal to drive under the influence of drugs
If I drive under the influence of drugs, I am punished in the same way as for drunk driving
aciklama: Drugs can remain in the blood for a long time. As long as they can be detected in the blood, it is forbidden to drive, and this is judged in the same way as drunk driving.

soru: The police stop you when you are driving tired late at night. Can you be punished?
secenekler: Yes, but only if I have also been drinking alcohol the same evening
Yes, if I cause an accident due to fatigue
No
aciklama: If a driver causes an accident due to fatigue, this is considered equivalent to driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs and can lead to punishment.

soru: How can you find out if a medicine affects your driving?
secenekler: There is a warning symbol on the medicine packaging
The pharmacy must inform about this and has full responsibility
It is stated in the medicine's package leaflet
aciklama: Side effects and how the medicine affects you as a driver are stated in the package leaflet. The pharmacy should inform, but the responsibility for finding out the side effects lies entirely with you (the driver).

soru: You are going to drive a long distance home at night. When are you likely to be most tired?
secenekler: Near home, at the end of the journey
At the beginning of the journey
In the middle of the journey
aciklama: Be especially aware of symptoms of fatigue, especially towards the end of the journey. If you notice you are starting to get tired, you can for example stop and stretch your legs or sleep for a short while.

soru: You have drunk quite a lot of alcohol late at night. What should you consider the day after?
secenekler: I should drink plenty of water and exercise before driving, as this speeds up metabolism
As long as I sleep a few hours before driving, I can drive the next day
I should eat a large breakfast before driving, as this speeds up metabolism
For safety reasons, I should not drive at all the day after, as alcohol may still be in the body
aciklama: Alcohol is metabolised relatively slowly, and it is difficult to know when all alcohol is gone from the body. Therefore, you should refrain from driving the day after.

soru: If you are stopped by the police for aggravated drunk driving, what is the most common penalty?
secenekler: Driving licence revoked and imprisonment
Only driving licence revoked
Driving licence revoked and a fine
aciklama: Aggravated drunk driving is 1.0 per mille.

soru: You have 0.1 per mille alcohol in your blood. Can you be convicted of drunk driving?
secenekler: No, the limit for drunk driving is 0.2 per mille
Yes, if you cannot drive the car safely
aciklama: Even if you are under 0.2 per mille (the limit for drunk driving), you can be convicted of drunk driving if you drive the car in a reckless or dangerous manner.

soru: Can you in any way speed up the metabolism of alcohol in the body?
secenekler: No
Yes, by eating a large meal with a lot of fat
Yes, by taking a sauna
Yes, by drinking coffee
aciklama: Regardless of which method is used, it is impossible to influence (speed up) the metabolism of alcohol in the body.

soru: How are you affected as a driver after drinking 50 cl of strong beer?
secenekler: I see double
I have difficulty keeping a straight course
I lose all judgement
My reaction time is prolonged
aciklama: Reaction time is affected already after one strong beer, while the other alternatives usually occur after greater alcohol consumption.

soru: What is the limit for drunk driving?
secenekler: 0.1 per mille
0.2 per mille
0.5 per mille
0.8 per mille
aciklama: The limit for drunk driving is 0.2 per mille. The limit for aggravated drunk driving is 1.0 per mille.

soru: If you drive after drinking a 33 cl strong beer (5%), can you be convicted of drunk driving?
secenekler: No, never
Yes, always
It varies from person to person
aciklama: How much alcohol you get in your blood is affected by many factors such as health, weight, gender, and how used you are to alcohol. Therefore, it is difficult to know how much alcohol is needed to reach 0.2 per mille. It varies from person to person. If you know you are going to drive, refrain from alcohol completely!

soru: Approximately what percentage of drivers killed in single-vehicle accidents were under the influence of alcohol?
secenekler: Approximately 30%
Approximately 50%
Approximately 70%
Approximately 90%
aciklama: You can read more in the Driving Licence Book Driving Theory 2026, page 164.

soru: You have drunk 14 cl of spirits (40%). How many 50 cl strong beers (5.6%) does this correspond to?
secenekler: Approximately one strong beer
Approximately two strong beers
Approximately three strong beers
Approximately four strong beers
aciklama: A rule of thumb: 50 cl strong beer (approx. 5.6%) corresponds to approximately 7 cl spirits (40%). Therefore, 14 cl spirits corresponds to two strong beers. Calculation: 14 cl spirits (40%) = 14 x 0.4 = 5.6 cl pure alcohol. 1 strong beer, 50 cl (5.6%) = 50 x 0.056 = 2.8 cl pure alcohol. Alcohol in spirits / alcohol in beer -> 5.6 ÷ 2.8 = 2.

soru: Does your health and weight affect how intoxicated you become from alcohol?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: How intoxicated you become is affected by several factors such as health, weight, gender, and how used you are to alcohol. Therefore, it is difficult to know how much alcohol is needed to reach 0.2 per mille.

soru: In which situation is the risk greatest that a driver is affected by peer pressure?
secenekler: When a man drives a car with girls in the car
When a man drives a car with other guys in the car
When a girl drives a car with guys in the car
When a girl drives a car with other girls in the car
aciklama: According to statistics and research, the risk is greatest that young male drivers are exposed to peer pressure and exhibit risk behaviour when they have other guys of their own age in the car. Read more in the Driving Licence Book, page 168.

soru: How does stress affect a driver?
secenekler: Stress never affects a driver's driving ability
Stress always has a negative effect on driving ability
Stress can impair my situational awareness
aciklama: When situational awareness is impaired, it becomes more difficult to detect things in your surroundings, which can lead to you missing, for example, a moose about to cross the road.

soru: How are drivers generally affected by stress?
secenekler: A driver's driving ability can improve with mild stress
A driver's driving ability is always negatively affected by stress
A driver's driving ability is not affected by stress
aciklama: Stress generally affects driving ability, but the effect is not always negative. Mild stress can increase performance and focus, while very high stress significantly impairs driving ability. Read more in the Driving Licence Book, page 170.

soru: How does peer pressure affect a driver's behaviour?
secenekler: Peer pressure always affects a driver negatively
Peer pressure never affects people with low self-esteem
If the group shows that it does not accept the driver breaking traffic rules, peer pressure can affect the driver positively
aciklama: Peer pressure often affects drivers, especially young ones. This pressure can be negative, but as in this example, it can also be positive by encouraging the driver to follow the rules.

soru: Which of the following is a consequence of peer pressure?
secenekler: That I drive my friends home from the party despite being under the influence of alcohol, even though I do not want to
That I increase speed despite my friends asking me to slow down
That I drive home tired in the evening despite my friends telling me not to
aciklama: In a group with poor dynamics, you may lack the courage to stand up for your own opinion. You do as everyone else and follow peer pressure. In this scenario, you would normally not have driven home under the influence if your friends had not persuaded you.

soru: Does your self-esteem have any significance for how easily you are affected by peer pressure?
secenekler: Yes, with good self-esteem I give in more easily to peer pressure
Yes, with good self-esteem it is easier to resist peer pressure
No, regardless of self-esteem, everyone gives in equally easily to peer pressure
aciklama: People with high self-esteem and self-confidence can more easily stand by their own decisions and resist the group's incorrect or risky demands. Read more in the Driving Licence Book, page 168.

soru: Which of the following makes you behave more safely in traffic?
secenekler: That I am stressed
That I have good self-control
That I overestimate my driving ability
That I am impulsive
aciklama: Good self-control affects you positively as a driver. The other alternatives generally have a negative effect on your driving. Read more about personality traits in the Driving Licence Book, page 173.

soru: Why do impulsive drivers tend to be dangerous in traffic?
secenekler: They often exceed speed limits
They take traffic rules lightly
They have low self-confidence as drivers
They often make sudden manoeuvres in traffic without thinking about the consequences
aciklama: "An impulsive person acts first and thinks later. These people can be very dangerous in traffic because they are unpredictable and surprise other drivers." (Driving Licence Book, page 174).

soru: What is the consequence of making excuses for your mistakes when driving?
secenekler: It is positive because it removes focus from mistakes in traffic
It is negative because my self-awareness increases
It is negative because I cannot learn from my mistakes
It is positive because my self-confidence increases and I become safer in traffic
aciklama: "We do not want to appear bad or admit that we have made a mistake. Often we try to find excuses and blame others. If 'it is never your fault' and you constantly make excuses, you lose the opportunity to learn from your mistakes." (Driving Licence Book, page 173).

soru: Can you lose your driving licence if you violate a stop obligation (stop sign)?
secenekler: Yes
No, the maximum penalty is a fine
aciklama: The driving licence is not always revoked, but depending on the traffic situation, such a penalty may be imposed.

soru: How long is the probationary period for a B driving licence?
secenekler: 1 year
2 years
5 years
10 years
aciklama: "You have a two-year probationary period from the date you received your driving licence. This means that if your driving licence is revoked during this time, you must retake the driving test." (Driving Licence Book, page 11).

soru: Who is responsible when you practice driving privately (e.g. with a parent)?
secenekler: All responsibility lies with me
All responsibility lies with the parent (supervisor)
All responsibility lies with the car's owner
Both have equal responsibility
aciklama: "During practice driving, the responsibility lies with the supervisor and they are legally considered the driver of the vehicle. This means that if an accident occurs or if you violate traffic rules during practice, it is the supervisor who has to face the consequences." (Driving Licence Book, page 9).

soru: In which of the following cases is the risk greatest that your driving licence will be revoked?
secenekler: When I drive at 135 km/h on a road with a 110 km/h limit
When I drive at 53 km/h on a road with a 30 km/h limit
When I do not give way when exiting a main road
When I change lanes on the motorway without signalling
aciklama: "As a general rule, you can expect your driving licence to be revoked if you exceed the speed limit by more than 20 km/h on a road with a 30 km/h limit, or by more than 30 km/h on roads with a higher speed limit." (Driving Licence Book, page 175). Alternatives three and four are considered minor violations and the risk of licence revocation is low.

soru: Can you be punished if you lend your car to someone you know does not have a driving licence?
secenekler: No
Yes
aciklama: This is considered 'allowing illegal driving' and can lead to a fine for the person lending the car.

soru: Can your driving licence be revoked if you are repeatedly taken into custody by the police due to intoxication (alcohol), even if you have never driven a car under the influence?
secenekler: No, the driving licence can only be revoked if I drive a car under the influence
Yes
aciklama: An example of when the Swedish Transport Agency can revoke your driving licence: "If you have repeatedly been taken into custody by the police due to intoxication. It does not have to be related to driving." (Driving Licence Book, page 176).

soru: You have attached a trailer to the car and are going to reverse. You ask someone else to keep watch behind the car and help you. If an accident occurs, who bears the responsibility?
secenekler: Both have joint responsibility
All responsibility lies with me
All responsibility lies with the person helping/keeping watch
aciklama: Even if you ask someone to keep watch behind the car, it is you who is driving and controlling the vehicle, and therefore you as the driver have all the responsibility.

soru: At which of the following ages is the risk of being killed in traffic the highest?
secenekler: 30 years
40 years
60 years
80 years
aciklama: "After the age of 75, the accident risk is five to six times higher compared to experienced and middle-aged drivers." (Driving Licence Book, page 179).

soru: Which type of accident is most common among older drivers?
secenekler: Intersection accidents
Single-vehicle accidents (run-off-road, etc.)
Wildlife accidents
Accidents in darkness/night-time
