aciklama: "Statistically, the accident risk increases again after the age of 75. These older drivers often have problems in traffic situations that require quick decisions and a lot of information, for example at intersections." (Driving Licence Book, page 180).

soru: Which statement about inexperienced drivers is correct?
secenekler: They often focus their gaze further ahead
They often have a more mobile eye sweep
They often focus their gaze close to the car
aciklama: "New drivers: keep their gaze very close to the car, focus more on stationary objects, are more passive, and sweep over a smaller area." (Driving Licence Book, page 184).

soru: You have recently obtained your driving licence. How can you best avoid being involved in an accident?
secenekler: By keeping large safety margins and driving defensively
By only driving when visibility conditions are good
By driving in difficult traffic conditions to develop my skills
By always driving slowly
aciklama: When you have recently obtained your driving licence and have little experience, it is difficult to assess risks in traffic. Therefore, it is important to be calm, plan your driving, and keep large safety margins.

soru: According to accident statistics, which of the following drivers is at greatest risk of being killed in traffic?
secenekler: A 20-year-old driver
A 30-year-old driver
A 45-year-old driver
A 60-year-old driver
aciklama: "It is important to be able to read traffic situations and foresee dangers. In the beginning, when you lack experience, this is difficult. [...] For young and new drivers, the accident risk is significantly higher than for experienced and middle-aged drivers." (Driving Licence Book, page 177).

soru: Which statement about young men and women in traffic is correct?
secenekler: There is no difference in accident statistics between young men and women
Young men are involved in fewer accidents than young women
Young women are involved in fewer accidents than young men
aciklama: "When examining drivers aged 18-19, one sees that the accident risk is six to seven times higher than for experienced and middle-aged drivers. Accident statistics also show that there are differences between genders and that women are involved in fewer accidents than men." (Driving Licence Book, page 178).

soru: Which statement about a driver with good self-awareness is correct?
secenekler: The driver often underestimates the dangers in traffic
The driver often takes risks
The driver can better assess the dangers in traffic
aciklama: Good self-awareness means that you as a driver do not overestimate your own driving skills, but are aware of your knowledge and abilities. A driver with high self-awareness can better assess dangers in traffic and therefore takes fewer risks.

soru: Where should you direct your gaze when driving a car?
secenekler: I should direct my gaze as far ahead as possible
I should direct my gaze close to the car
aciklama: To detect important information and dangers in time, it is important to have a mobile gaze and direct it far ahead.

soru: Which of the following statements about our vision is correct?
secenekler: When vision deteriorates, it happens gradually, so we do not notice it immediately
Older people often have better night vision
Drivers who wear glasses must have an eye test every five years
All drivers must have an eye test every ten years
aciklama: Since it can be difficult to notice when vision deteriorates, it can be a good idea to have your eyes checked regularly as you get older.

soru: Which statement about how you focus/direct your gaze is correct?
secenekler: If I fix my gaze on a single object, there is a great risk that I will miss other important information
If I fix my gaze on the car in front, it becomes easier to avoid dangers
If I fix my gaze just in front of the car, it becomes easier to detect dangers
As a rule, experienced drivers keep their gaze just in front of the car
aciklama: To detect important information and dangers in time, it is important to have a mobile gaze and direct it far ahead.

soru: After you have obtained your B driving licence, when are you legally required to have an eye test?
secenekler: Every two years
Every five years
Every year after you turn 70
Never
aciklama: According to the law, you are not obliged to have a new eye test after obtaining your driving licence, regardless of age. But since sharp vision is very important for driving, it is recommended that you check your eyes.

soru: How does alcohol affect your vision?
secenekler: My field of vision widens
I detect moving objects around me more easily
My peripheral vision is impaired
My central vision becomes sharper
aciklama: We detect moving objects with our peripheral vision, which constitutes approximately 98-99% of our field of vision. If you drive after drinking alcohol, your peripheral vision is impaired and you become less aware of your surroundings.

soru: How do central and peripheral vision work?
secenekler: Central vision has poorer sharpness and constitutes the largest part of the field of vision
Central vision has good sharpness and constitutes only a small part of the field of vision
Peripheral vision has good sharpness and constitutes only a small part of the field of vision
Peripheral vision has poorer sharpness and constitutes only a small part of the field of vision
aciklama: Central vision: Has good visual acuity and constitutes approximately 1-2% of the field of vision. Peripheral vision: Has poorer visual acuity and constitutes approximately 98-99% of the field of vision. You detect objects in your surroundings, especially moving ones, with your peripheral vision.

soru: You are driving at 110 km/h on the motorway and turn off onto an exit ramp. The speed limit on the ramp is 50 km/h. If you do not look at the speedometer, what are you likely to do?
secenekler: You reduce speed too little and drive faster than 50 km/h
You reduce speed too much and drive slower than 50 km/h
You reduce speed to 70 km/h because the speed on the exit ramp is only a recommendation
aciklama: It is easy to suffer from speed blindness on the motorway. Speed blindness makes you feel that you are driving slower than you actually are. Therefore, if you do not look at the speedometer, you will likely not reduce your speed enough.

soru: You have decided to overtake a vehicle in front of you. What is most difficult to assess in this situation?
secenekler: Estimating the speed of the vehicle you are overtaking
Estimating the speed of the oncoming vehicle
Estimating when you have passed the vehicle you are overtaking
aciklama: Since it is difficult to estimate the speed of an oncoming vehicle, it is also difficult to judge when you will meet it. Therefore, you should not overtake if there is oncoming traffic, because the risk is too great. If you spot an oncoming vehicle during the overtaking, you should be prepared to abort the overtaking.

soru: Is the risk of tunnel vision affected by speed?
secenekler: Yes, the risk of tunnel vision increases at lower speeds
Yes, the risk of tunnel vision increases at higher speeds
No, tunnel vision is only affected by the driver's condition
No, tunnel vision is only affected by visibility conditions
aciklama: "Tunnel vision occurs when you drive at high speed. Your search field narrows and your ability to perceive things at the roadside deteriorates." (Driving Licence Book, page 189).

soru: You notice that the car pulls to one side when driving. What could this be due to?
secenekler: That one of the front tyres has too low air pressure
That both front tyres have too high air pressure
That both rear tyres have too high air pressure
aciklama: To avoid such situations, you should regularly check the tyre air pressure. Correct tyre pressure also contributes to lower fuel consumption.

soru: What can cause tunnel vision?
secenekler: When I come out of a dark tunnel and am dazzled by bright light
When I drive a long distance in a tunnel
When I am affected by stress or fatigue
When I drive into a tunnel
aciklama: "Fatigue, stress, and alcohol can also affect the search field and cause tunnel vision." (Driving Licence Book, page 189).

soru: Which of our senses do we use most in traffic?
secenekler: Touch
Hearing
Smell
Sight
aciklama: "90% of the information in traffic we take in with our sight, and 10% with our other senses." (Driving Licence Book, page 188).

soru: Which of the following situations increases the risk of speed blindness?
secenekler: When I drive in a built-up area
When I drive a noisy car
When I drive on a pedestrian street
When I drive a quiet car
aciklama: "When the road is wide and straight, the brain does not get enough sensory input and the risk of speed blindness increases. Quiet cars also increase this risk, because the engine is one of the impressions the brain uses to estimate speed." (Driving Licence Book, page 188).

soru: You have been driving at high speed for a long time and have suffered from speed blindness. What is the greatest risk with speed blindness?
secenekler: That I drive too slowly if I do not look at the speedometer
That I get shorter visibility
That I underestimate the car's braking distance
That I miss traffic signs
aciklama: "Speed blindness means you have difficulty estimating what speed you are keeping and that you feel you are driving slower than you actually are. This can lead to you underestimating the braking distance, not reducing speed enough, and driving off the road when you try to brake on an exit ramp." (Driving Licence Book, page 188).

soru: School buses have warning lights that flash to draw your attention to the fact that the bus is going to stop and drop off students. When do these lights turn on?
secenekler: Immediately before the bus stop
Approximately 10 metres before the bus stop
Approximately 100 metres before the bus stop
It varies depending on the applicable speed limit
aciklama: "Cars and buses transporting children to school are equipped with a special sign with orange flashing lights. When these vehicles are about to drop off passengers, the flashing lights turn on to draw attention from other road users. The lights turn on 100 metres before the stopping place and remain on throughout the stop. They only turn off 100 metres after the stopping place." (Driving Licence Book, page 193).

soru: Which statement about road users with hidden/invisible disabilities is most correct?
secenekler: They always wear reflectors so that I can easily spot them
They are often more careful due to their disabilities, so they are rarely involved in accidents
They always have a guide dog or white cane, so they are easy to spot
It can be difficult to detect their disability
aciklama: There are many disabilities that are not visible externally, such as hearing impairment or mild visual impairment. It can be more difficult for these people to manage in traffic, and it is not easy for drivers to detect this from the outside.

soru: Which statement about children's behaviour in traffic is correct?
secenekler: They have good hearing and can therefore detect vehicles more easily
They have faster reflexes than adults and are therefore rarely involved in accidents
They are impulsive and unpredictable
aciklama: Children almost always play and rarely think before they act. Their hearing is not yet fully developed and they may have difficulty assessing risks. This makes them impulsive and unpredictable in traffic.

soru: A vehicle with this sign is standing at the roadside and its lights are flashing yellow. What applies in this situation?
secenekler: I have to give way when the driver pulls out from the roadside
I must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing
I can drive past the vehicle as long as I drive calmly and slowly
aciklama: You do not have to give way and do not need to stop, but since there may be children who have disembarked near the vehicle, you should drive calmly and slowly.

soru: What is most difficult to detect when reversing a car?
secenekler: Children approaching from the side
Cyclists approaching straight from behind
Children approaching diagonally from behind
Cyclists approaching from the side
aciklama: Children are small and therefore difficult to detect. When reversing, the most difficult road users to detect are children approaching diagonally from behind.

soru: How do children differ from adults in traffic?
secenekler: There is not much difference
Children's hearing is not fully developed
Children move more, so they are easier to detect
Children have a less limited field of vision
aciklama: Since children's hearing develops during childhood, they have more difficulty determining where a sound is coming from. This makes it harder for them to handle traffic situations.

soru: Which statement about the elderly in traffic is correct?
secenekler: They understand traffic rules poorly
Elderly pedestrians often have a slower pace
They are often involved in single-vehicle accidents
aciklama: Elderly road users do not have worse understanding of traffic rules and do not break the rules more often than younger drivers. Their mobility, vision, and hearing are often impaired, which means they often have a slower pace.

soru: Does your choice of gear affect fuel consumption?
secenekler: No, which gear I choose does not affect fuel consumption
Yes, driving in as low a gear as possible reduces fuel consumption
Yes, driving in as high a gear as possible reduces fuel consumption
aciklama: To reduce fuel consumption: "Drive in high gear. Shift up early and then drive in as high a gear as possible. In many new petrol cars, it is appropriate to drive in fifth gear already at 50–60 km/h." (Driving Licence Book, page 201).

soru: How can you best reduce your fuel consumption and thus your environmental impact through your choice of route?
secenekler: I choose a road where I can maintain a steady speed
I choose a road where I often have to accelerate and brake
I choose the road with the lowest speed limit
I choose a road where I have to stop regularly
aciklama: Braking and accelerating increase fuel consumption, so a road where you can maintain a steady speed is best from an environmental perspective.

soru: You are approaching an intersection where you are going to turn. Which driving technique is best from an environmental perspective?
secenekler: Use only the foot brake before the turn
Press the clutch and put it in neutral before the turn
Increase speed just before the turn
Engine brake (shift down) before the turn
aciklama: During engine braking, no fuel is used to drive the engine's cylinders; they are driven by the vehicle's kinetic energy. Since no fuel is combusted, emissions are reduced.

soru: From an environmental perspective, is it best to start the engine before scraping the windows?
secenekler: Yes, then the engine has time to warm up before driving and fuel consumption is reduced
No, it increases fuel consumption
It makes no difference
aciklama: Warming the engine with an engine heater before starting is a good idea because cold starts increase fuel consumption. But letting the engine idle to warm it up before driving increases emissions, because the engine is running but you are not driving and fuel is being consumed unnecessarily.

soru: How can you reduce your harmful exhaust emissions?
secenekler: I maintain a steady speed and drive at low revs
I start in high gear
I constantly drive in low gear
I try to engine brake as little as possible
aciklama: If you accelerate and brake often, fuel consumption increases. Try therefore to maintain a steady speed. Some cars have cruise control that helps maintain a steady speed. The higher the engine revs, the more fuel the engine consumes. Therefore, drive in as high a gear as possible.

soru: How do you engine brake?
secenekler: I release the accelerator pedal and shift down
I brake gently and shift down
I brake gently and shift up
I release the accelerator pedal and keep the clutch pressed down
aciklama: Engine braking: "When you completely release the accelerator pedal with the engine speed above 1500–1600 rpm, no fuel is supplied to the engine. When the rpm drops to 1200–1300 rpm, the engine starts consuming fuel again. To maintain zero fuel consumption, shift down just before the rpm reaches 1200–1300. Repeat this downshift."

soru: Which fuel contributes least to carbon dioxide emissions?
secenekler: Natural gas
Diesel
Petrol
Biogas
aciklama: "Biofuels, unlike fossil fuels, have the advantage that they do not contribute to the greenhouse effect because they are produced from plants. The amount of carbon dioxide released during combustion is the same as the plant absorbed before it was harvested." (Driving Licence Book, page 204).

soru: Which fuel is not renewable?
secenekler: Biogas
Ethanol
Petrol
aciklama: Both ethanol and biogas are renewable. Petrol is a fossil fuel, which means it is not renewable. Read more about environmentally friendly fuels in the Driving Licence Book, page 204.

soru: Which substance in car exhaust reduces the blood's ability to transport oxygen?
secenekler: Benzene
Carbon monoxide
Hydrogen
Carbon dioxide
aciklama: "Carbon monoxide reduces the blood's oxygen uptake capacity, leading to fatigue and concentration difficulties. The gas is odourless and colourless, and in high doses life-threatening." (Driving Licence Book, page 205).

soru: Which tyre type causes the most dangerous particles to be released from the road surface (wears most on the road)?
secenekler: Summer tyres
Studded tyres
Friction tyres/winter tyres
aciklama: "Soot and particles can cause respiratory problems and increase the risk of cancer. Soot and particles are one of the biggest problems in urban environments. These particles are formed through combustion in engines and through road wear caused by studded tyres." (Driving Licence Book, page 206). These particles also damage the environment.

soru: Which of the following substances contributes most to acidification and eutrophication in nature?
secenekler: Nitrogen oxide
Carbon dioxide
Hydrocarbons
aciklama: "Nitrogen oxides together with hydrocarbons form ground-level ozone. The oxides contribute to the acidification of nature and eutrophication of seas and lakes. They also irritate mucous membranes and affect the respiratory tract." (Driving Licence Book, page 206).

soru: Car exhaust contributes to the greenhouse effect. Which substance in the exhaust has the greatest impact on the greenhouse effect?
secenekler: Nitrogen oxide
Carbon monoxide
Carbon dioxide
Benzene
aciklama: All substances in the alternatives are harmful to the environment or health, but carbon dioxide undoubtedly has the greatest impact on the greenhouse effect.

soru: What percentage of Sweden's total carbon dioxide emissions comes from road traffic?
secenekler: Approximately 80%
Approximately 60%
Approximately 30%
Approximately 10%
aciklama: Approximately 30 percent of Sweden's total carbon dioxide emissions come from the road transport sector (lorries, buses, passenger cars and motorcycles).

soru: Which tax is paid based on the vehicle's carbon dioxide emissions?
secenekler: VAT
Congestion tax
Vehicle tax
aciklama: Vehicle tax is determined based on the vehicle's fuel type and carbon dioxide emissions.

soru: Does a roof box (roof rack) affect fuel consumption?
secenekler: No, it does not affect it
Yes, but only if the roof box is loaded
Yes, always
aciklama: A roof box increases the car's air resistance and thus increases fuel consumption.

soru: How is fuel consumption affected if you drive with too low tyre pressure?
secenekler: It decreases
It is not affected
It increases
aciklama: To reduce fuel consumption, it is important to regularly check tyre pressure. Low tyre pressure leads to increased fuel consumption and poorer road grip.

soru: How does four-wheel drive affect fuel consumption compared to front- or rear-wheel drive?
secenekler: Four-wheel drive reduces fuel consumption
Four-wheel drive does not affect fuel consumption
Four-wheel drive increases fuel consumption
aciklama: Four-wheel drive cars generally consume more fuel (approximately 5% more).

soru: From an environmental perspective, you should not wash your car in an asphalted driveway that slopes towards the street. Why?
secenekler: When I wash the car myself, more water is used than in a professional car wash
Chemicals and oil residues run down into the street drains and further to the nearest watercourse
Car cleaning products evaporate and contribute to the greenhouse effect
The street is damaged by the chemicals running from the car
aciklama: Car care products are environmentally hazardous and should not be flushed down street drains or into the ground. Street drains lead stormwater directly to the nearest watercourse without treatment. The best option is to wash at a place with an oil separator, for example a do-it-yourself car wash facility.

soru: Which statement about engine heaters is correct?
secenekler: It increases fuel consumption
It has a negative environmental impact
It does not work at temperatures below minus five degrees
It reduces fuel consumption
aciklama: During cold starts, fuel consumption increases. Using an engine heater before starting therefore reduces fuel consumption.

soru: Which of the following options does not affect fuel consumption?
secenekler: The car's weight
Air conditioning
Mounted roof box
The condition of the brakes
aciklama: The car's weight, use of air conditioning, and roof box directly increase fuel consumption, while the condition of the brakes does not affect fuel consumption.

soru: When the temperature is zero degrees, how long before starting should you turn on the engine heater?
secenekler: 10 minutes
30 minutes
One hour
Two hours
aciklama: How long the engine heater should be connected depends on the outside temperature. Approximate times: -15°C -> 90 minutes, 0°C -> 60 minutes, 10°C -> 30 minutes.

soru: From an environmental perspective, is it good to wax the car?
secenekler: Yes
No
aciklama: If you wax the car, dirt does not stick as easily, which means you do not need to wash the car as often. Therefore, it is good from an environmental perspective to wax the car.

soru: What percentage of the car's carbon dioxide is cleaned by the catalytic converter?
aciklama: The catalytic converter cleans the exhaust gases from harmful substances. The catalytic converter converts approximately 80-95% of the harmful substances into carbon dioxide and water, which means that carbon dioxide emissions are not reduced. This is a problem that can only be solved by reducing fuel consumption.

soru: If you buy a new petrol passenger car, must it be equipped with a catalytic converter?
secenekler: No, but it is recommended for less environmental impact
Yes
aciklama: All petrol cars manufactured today must be equipped with a catalytic converter. The catalytic converter cleans the exhaust gases from toxic substances.

soru: Which traffic sign warns of a pedestrian crossing ahead?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign A is 'Warning for pedestrian crossing'. Triangular warning signs indicate a danger or a situation ahead. Sign B indicates the pedestrian crossing itself, C warns of children, and D indicates a footpath.

soru: What does this traffic sign mean?
secenekler: I should apply the right-hand rule
All traffic on the intersecting road must give way to me
I must give way to all traffic on the intersecting road
aciklama: The sign is 'Warning for intersection with give way obligation'. In this intersection, traffic on the main road (the thick line) has priority.

soru: You see this traffic sign while driving. What should you be prepared for?
secenekler: That a gentle curve is coming
That the number of lanes is decreasing
That the road narrows from both sides
That the road narrows from the right side
aciklama: The sign is 'Warning for road with narrower carriageway from both sides'. It indicates that the road will narrow from both the right and left, and drivers should adjust their speed and be attentive.

soru: You are driving on a motorway at 110 km/h and see a warning sign. How far is it to the hazard?
secenekler: 50 - 100 metres
100 - 200 metres
200 - 400 metres
400 - 500 metres
aciklama: The distance to the hazard varies depending on the speed limit: 50 km/h or lower: 5–75 metres; 60 or 70 km/h: 50–200 metres; 80 or 90 km/h: 150–250 metres; higher than 90 km/h: 200–400 metres.

soru: What does this traffic sign mean?
secenekler: Warning for cycle path parallel to your road
Warning for cyclists
That I must give way to all cyclists
aciklama: The sign is 'Warning for cyclists and moped riders'. It indicates that cyclists or moped riders may cross or enter the road ahead, and drivers should be attentive.

soru: What does this combination of traffic signs mean?
secenekler: That a 1.5 kilometre long winding road begins after 200 metres
That a dangerous right curve begins after 200 metres, followed by a 1.5 kilometre long winding road
That a dangerous right curve begins after 200 metres, followed by a 1.3 kilometre long winding road
That a dangerous left curve begins after 200 metres, followed by a 1.3 kilometre long winding road
aciklama: The upper sign is 'Warning for several dangerous curves, first curve to the right'. The supplementary plate below shows where the hazard begins and ends. The dangerous, winding road begins 200 metres after the traffic sign and ends 1.5 kilometres further ahead. This means the length of the winding road is 1.3 kilometres (1.5 - 0.2 = 1.3).

soru: After which traffic sign does the right-hand rule apply?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign C is 'Warning for intersection' and indicates that the right-hand rule applies at the upcoming intersection. A shows a main road, B shows give way, and D warns of an intersection where the main road turns.

soru: You are driving on a road with a 50 km/h limit. What does the sign warn of and how far is it to the intersection?
secenekler: Manned railway crossing at 50–200 metres
Manned railway crossing at 5–75 metres
Unmanned railway crossing at 50–200 metres
Unmanned railway crossing at 5–75 metres
aciklama: The sign is 'Warning for unmanned railway crossing'. On roads with a speed limit of 50 km/h or lower, warning signs are placed approximately 5–75 metres before the hazard.

soru: You pass this traffic sign while driving. What does it mean?
secenekler: That stopping is prohibited
That the main road ends
That parking is prohibited
That the main road continues
aciklama: The sign is 'End of main road'. It indicates that the main road status ends and that the right-hand rule may apply at upcoming intersections unless otherwise stated.

soru: You encounter this combination. Which is correct?
secenekler: I must stop immediately before the track
If there is no stop line, I must stop 10 metres before the track
If there is no stop line, I must stop level with the STOP sign
I only need to stop if a train is coming
aciklama: There is a sign for a railway crossing with multiple tracks and a STOP sign underneath. Where there is a STOP sign, you must stop immediately before the road or track, and you have to give way to all vehicles in the intersection.

soru: A pedestrian is approaching from the right. Which rule applies?
secenekler: I have to give way to the pedestrian because the crossing is controlled
The pedestrian has to give way to me because the crossing is controlled
The pedestrian has to give way to me because they are standing at the kerb
I have to give way to the pedestrian because the crossing is uncontrolled
aciklama: When traffic lights are off/out of order, the crossing is considered uncontrolled. At uncontrolled pedestrian crossings, you have to give way to pedestrians who are about to or are crossing.

soru: Which traffic sign means that oncoming traffic must give way to you?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign B is 'Priority over oncoming traffic'. The white arrow on a blue background shows that you have priority and the red arrow shows that oncoming traffic must give way. A gives priority to oncoming traffic, C is give way, and D is an uncontrolled intersection.

soru: You come to a STOP sign and are standing behind another vehicle. When the vehicle in front has driven off, what should you do?
secenekler: I must stop again at my own stop line before driving out
I can drive directly after the vehicle in front without stopping
I can roll slowly and continue without stopping if nothing is coming from the intersecting road
aciklama: The stop obligation is individual. Even if you have stopped behind another vehicle, you must stop again at the stop line, or at the edge of the carriageway if no line exists, before you yourself drive out into the intersection.

soru: You are approaching this intersection. Which statement is correct?
secenekler: I must stop before entering the intersecting road
I only have to give way to traffic from the right
I have to give way to all traffic on the intersecting road
aciklama: The sign is 'Give way'. When you see this sign, you must yield to all traffic on the intersecting road, both from the right and left. Unlike the STOP sign, you do not need to stop completely if the road is clear and the traffic situation allows.

soru: According to the signs in the picture, which is correct?
secenekler: Both A and B mean that the road is one-way
B means that the road is one-way
B means that the road is closed to all traffic in both directions
aciklama: Sign A: 'Motor traffic prohibited' - entry prohibited from both directions. Sign B: 'Entry prohibited' - vehicles may not enter from this side, but traffic can flow from the other direction. This means the road is one-way.

soru: Which statement about the traffic sign is correct?
secenekler: I may park for a maximum of 10 minutes
I may only stop for loading/unloading
I may neither park nor stop
aciklama: The sign means 'No stopping and no parking'. It is forbidden to park and also to stop temporarily, including for dropping off passengers or loading.

soru: What applies in the situation shown in the picture?
secenekler: 50 km/h is the recommended maximum speed
The toll is 50 kronor
The speed limit is 50 km/h
Roadworks after 50 metres
aciklama: Electronic speed signs without a red border do not indicate a legal speed limit, but the 'recommended maximum speed' for the prevailing traffic conditions. You are recommended to drive at a maximum of 50 km/h, but if weather and road conditions permit, you may legally drive faster.

soru: You pass this traffic sign. Is it allowed to park?
secenekler: Yes, in marked parking spaces
Yes, after the next intersection
No, never
aciklama: The sign is a 'Zone' sign. It means that a parking ban applies throughout the zone until you see an 'End of zone' sign. You may however park in specially marked parking spaces within the zone.

soru: Which of the following traffic signs usually ceases to apply after the next intersection?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign C (No stopping and no parking) usually applies until the next intersection, unless a supplementary sign indicates otherwise. Sign A (speed limit) applies until a new speed sign is shown; B (pedestrian zone) and D (parking ban zone) apply until their respective end signs.

soru: Fill in the blank: Vehicles with _________ over 13 tonnes may not pass this sign.
secenekler: Total weight
Maximum load
Kerb weight
Gross weight
aciklama: The sign is 'Limited gross vehicle weight'. Gross weight is the vehicle's actual weight at a specific time (kerb weight + current load). If the vehicle's weighed actual weight exceeds 13 tonnes, it is forbidden to enter the road.

soru: Is it allowed to overtake other vehicles after this traffic sign?
secenekler: Yes, but only two-wheeled vehicles
No, never
Yes, always
aciklama: The sign is 'No overtaking'. After this sign, it is forbidden for motor vehicles to overtake each other. Exception: You may overtake two-wheeled motor vehicles (e.g. motorcycles or mopeds without sidecars).

soru: The pictures show the back of traffic signs. Which option shows 'Entry prohibited'?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: The only sign that is curved/turned in the picture is 'Entry prohibited' (option C). When you see the back of this sign in traffic, you understand that the road you are on is one-way and that entry from the other direction is prohibited.

soru: You are driving on a road with a 70 km/h limit. How long does this traffic sign apply?
secenekler: Until its end sign
Until the next intersection
50-200 metres
200-400 metres
aciklama: The 'No overtaking' sign does not automatically end at intersections. The prohibition applies until you see a specific 'No overtaking ends' sign.

soru: At which sign is it not allowed to go straight ahead?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign C is 'Compulsory direction, right or left'. At the intersection with this sign, you must turn either right or left; it is absolutely forbidden to go straight ahead. A and B allow straight ahead, while D is a warning sign for an uncontrolled intersection.

soru: Which vehicles may pass this traffic sign?
secenekler: Only buses in line traffic
Buses in line traffic and all lorries
Buses in line traffic and all light motorcycles
Buses in line traffic and moped class II
aciklama: The sign is 'Carriageway or lane for line traffic etc.'. In addition to buses in line traffic, bicycles and moped class II are also allowed to use the road or lane.

soru: Which traffic sign means that you must go straight ahead at the next intersection?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign D is 'Compulsory direction, straight ahead'. It indicates that at the upcoming intersection, you may only go straight ahead and that turning right or left is prohibited.

soru: Which traffic sign indicates that you must drive into the left lane/side?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign D is 'Compulsory direction, left'. It indicates that you must pass the obstacle or division on the left side. A shows straight ahead or left, B shows only left, C shows that you can pass on both sides.

soru: You see this sign while driving. What does it mean?
secenekler: That a sharp right curve is ahead
That I must drive in the right lane
That I must turn right at the next intersection
That I can go straight ahead or turn right at the next intersection
aciklama: The sign is 'Compulsory direction, right turn'. It indicates that at the upcoming intersection, you are obliged to turn right. It is forbidden to go straight ahead or turn left.

soru: What applies for this traffic sign?
secenekler: The sign is a warning for off-road vehicles
I have to give way to all off-road vehicles
Pedestrians and off-road vehicles may pass
Only off-road vehicles may pass
aciklama: The sign is 'Compulsory carriageway for off-road motor vehicles and off-road trailers'. This road is specially intended for off-road vehicles such as snowmobiles. Pedestrians may however also use the road.

soru: Which statement about the area with this traffic sign is correct?
secenekler: This road may be used by cyclists, pedestrians, and also moped class II
This road may only be used by cyclists
This road may only be used by cyclists and pedestrians
This road may only be used by pedestrians
aciklama: The sign is 'Shared pedestrian and cycle path'. This road is intended for cyclists and pedestrians. Additionally, moped class II are allowed to use this road according to the rules.

soru: What is the basic speed limit within built-up areas?
secenekler: 30 km/h
50 km/h
60 km/h
70 km/h
aciklama: The basic speed limit within built-up areas is 50 km/h. Outside built-up areas, it is 70 km/h.

soru: What applies after the sign in the picture?
secenekler: The maximum permitted speed is 30 km/h
It is forbidden to drive faster than 30 km/h without creating danger
It is allowed to drive faster than 30 km/h without creating danger
aciklama: The blue sign with 'max 30 km/tim' is not a legal speed limit, but a 'Recommended low speed' sign. It is recommended that you drive at 30 km/h or lower for safe driving, but if the traffic situation allows and you do not endanger safety, it is legal to drive faster.

soru: What does the sign below the pedestrian crossing sign mean?
secenekler: That a T-junction is ahead
That the road is a dead end for me as a driver
That only cyclists and pedestrians may pass
aciklama: The sign below the pedestrian crossing is 'Dead end street'. It indicates that the road is a dead end for vehicle traffic. The supplementary sign shows that the road from a certain point becomes a cycle path and that motor traffic ends there.

soru: What is correct when you encounter this traffic sign?
secenekler: I must stop at the sign
This is a place where the road is extra wide to facilitate meetings
This sign is used to warn of oncoming traffic before curves on narrow roads
aciklama: The sign 'Meeting place' indicates that the road has been widened for vehicles to meet on narrow roads.

soru: After which traffic sign must you keep the lowest speed?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: Sign B is 'Pedestrian zone'. In this area, vehicles may only be driven at walking speed. This is the lowest speed limit among the alternatives. A is 30 km/h, C is recommended 20 km/h, and D is 50 km/h (built-up area).

soru: What does this traffic sign mean?
secenekler: Direction at road signs
One-way street
Dead end street
Compulsory direction, left
aciklama: The sign means 'One-way traffic'. It indicates that the street or road is one-way and that traffic may only flow in the direction of the arrow.

soru: What does this direction sign mean?
secenekler: Direction sign for motorway or motorway-like road
Direction sign for public road
Direction sign for private road
Direction sign for local destination
aciklama: The sign is 'Direction sign to local destination'. In Swedish traffic rules, direction signs with white background and black text are used for local destinations or neighbourhood areas. Blue signs are public roads, green are motorways, and yellow/red are private roads.

soru: What does this road sign inform about?
secenekler: Beach
Youth hostel
Outdoor recreation area
Industrial area
aciklama: The sign is 'Industrial area'. The blue background with a white square and factory symbol indicates that the area is an industrial area and leads to facilities in this area.

soru: If you want to go towards Boda, what type of turn must you make?
secenekler: Safe left turn
Spanish turn
U-turn
Regular left turn
aciklama: The sign shows a 'Spanish turn'. In this type of intersection, it is forbidden and dangerous to turn left directly from the main road. Instead, you turn onto a right slip road which then curves back and crosses the main road at a right angle. This way you can safely cross the road without blocking the traffic flow or making a risky left turn.

soru: What does this road sign mean?
secenekler: That I must turn right
Compulsory right turn
Temporary direction due to roadworks
That I am entering a private road if I turn right
aciklama: The sign is 'Temporary direction in current exit'. This orange arrow sign is used in roadworks areas to temporarily direct traffic to an alternative route or service road.

soru: What does this road sign mean?
secenekler: Direction sign for motorway or motorway-like road
Direction sign for public road
Direction sign for private road
Direction sign for local destination
aciklama: The sign is 'Direction sign for public road'. In Swedish traffic rules, direction signs with blue background and white text are used for public roads that are not motorways or motorway-like roads. The number indicates the distance to the destination in kilometres.

soru: Which localisation sign indicates a rest area?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: The meanings of the signs: A is information point, B is hotel, C is rest and recreation area, D is cottage/mountain cabin. The correct answer is therefore C.

soru: You are going to drive towards Sundsvall. Can you drive in the rightmost lane?
secenekler: No
Yes
aciklama: According to the lane guidance, you can use all three lanes to go towards Sundsvall. The arrow in the rightmost lane shows that it both goes straight ahead towards Sundsvall and turns off towards Enköping. You can therefore continue towards Sundsvall even from the rightmost lane.

soru: What does this road sign mean?
secenekler: Road number on motorway or motorway-like road
Direction sign: temporary exit/alternative route
Direction sign: private road
Exit number
aciklama: The sign is 'Exit number'. This oval sign with yellow background, black exit symbol and number is used to number specific exits on motorways and motorway-like roads. The purpose is to help drivers navigate and know which exit to take.

soru: What does this road sign mean?
secenekler: An advance direction sign showing road numbers
An advance direction sign showing speed limits
A lane guidance sign
A tabular direction sign with distance information
aciklama: The sign is an 'Advance direction sign'. These large blue signs are used before an intersection or road exit to inform drivers. They schematically show with arrows which roads lead to which main destinations and indicate road numbers.

soru: What does this combination of road signs mean?
secenekler: No stopping after the sign but not before
No stopping both before and after the sign
No parking both before and after the sign
No parking before the sign but not after
aciklama: The main sign is 'No parking'. The supplementary sign with a double arrow indicates that the prohibition applies both before and after the sign. It is therefore forbidden to park both in front of and behind the sign.

soru: You park your car on a Saturday at 7:00 PM. When is the latest you must collect the car?
secenekler: Saturday at 12:00 AM
Sunday at 8:00 AM
Sunday at 10:00 AM
Monday at 8:00 AM
aciklama: The main sign shows a parking ban, the supplementary sign shows when the ban applies. In Swedish traffic rules: Numbers without parentheses refer to weekdays, numbers within parentheses refer to Saturdays. Saturday's ban ends at 5:00 PM, so you park outside the ban period at 7:00 PM. On Sunday, no ban applies, so the car can remain. The ban starts again on Monday at 8:00 AM, so you must collect the car by Monday at 8:00 AM at the latest.

soru: Which statement is correct?
secenekler: You are driving on a motorway and in three kilometres a main road begins
A motorway is a main road and it begins in three kilometres
You are driving on a main road and in three kilometres a motorway begins
aciklama: The sign combination gives two pieces of information: The lower yellow-white diamond-shaped sign shows that you are on a main road. The upper green sign with the supplementary plate '3 km' indicates that the motorway begins in three kilometres. The correct answer is therefore the third alternative.

soru: Who may park in parking spaces for disabled people?
secenekler: Only people who use a walker
Only people with a special permit
Only people with a special medical certificate
Only people who are wheelchair dependent
aciklama: The sign is 'Parking for disabled people'. To park here, a valid special parking permit issued by the municipality is required. Using a walker or having a medical certificate is not sufficient. Without a permit, you may only stop temporarily to drop off or pick up passengers, but absolutely not park.

soru: Which rule applies after this combination of road signs?
secenekler: I may stop and park
I may not park
I may not stop
I may neither stop nor park
aciklama: The main sign is 'No stopping and no parking'. The supplementary sign with a downward-pointing arrow indicates that the prohibition ends at the sign's placement. Since the prohibition ends here, it is free to stop and park after the sign.

soru: When does the speed limit shown in the picture apply?
secenekler: All days 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
All days
Saturdays and Sundays 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Weekdays 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
aciklama: The main sign indicates 40 km/h, the supplementary sign indicates when the limit applies. In Swedish traffic rules: Numbers without parentheses on supplementary signs refer to weekdays (not public holidays). The speed limit therefore only applies on weekdays between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM.

soru: What should you be aware of when you see this sign combination?
secenekler: I should be careful with hearing-impaired children
I should be careful with visually impaired children
I should be careful with mobility-impaired children
aciklama: The upper main sign is 'Warning for children/school crossing'. The yellow supplementary sign with three black dots symbolises 'Hearing impairment/hearing impaired'. The combination warns that children in the area may have difficulty hearing approaching vehicles, which requires extra caution and low speed.

soru: What does the police signal mean?
secenekler: Stop for vehicles facing the police and for vehicles behind the police
Reduce speed
Stop for vehicles behind the police
Stop for vehicles facing the police
aciklama: The police officer's arm extended to the side in this position means an absolute stop for all vehicles approaching from both the front and the back of the police officer. Traffic that is level with the police officer's shoulders may continue.

soru: What does the police signal mean?
secenekler: Reduce speed for vehicles facing the police
Reduce speed for vehicles behind the police
Stop for vehicles behind the police
Stop for vehicles facing the police
aciklama: The police officer holds their arm outstretched at shoulder height and waves their palm downwards. This is an instruction to drivers approaching from the direction the police officer is facing (i.e. from the front) to reduce speed.

soru: If a road transport leader gives you an instruction, must you follow it?
secenekler: No
Yes
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, road transport leaders escorting long, heavy or wide special transports have the authority to give instructions to road users, just like a police officer. They are permitted to direct traffic to ensure the transport's progress and minimise disruptions. Therefore, it is mandatory to follow their signals and instructions.

soru: What does the police signal mean?
secenekler: Reduce speed for vehicles in the direction the police officer is pointing
Vehicles in the direction the police officer is pointing may continue driving
Stop for vehicles in the direction the police officer is pointing
aciklama: The police officer holds one arm outstretched to the side and makes a circular motion with the other hand or light at chest height in the direction of travel. This signal means that traffic in the indicated direction is permitted to pass. Vehicles in that direction may continue without stopping or reducing speed.

soru: What does the police signal mean?
secenekler: Vehicles behind the police car should follow and stop
Vehicles behind the police car should reduce speed
Vehicles in front of the police car should follow and stop
Vehicles in front of the police car should reduce speed
aciklama: The police officer extends a 'stop signal' through the window of the moving police car. This is directed at the driver driving immediately behind the police car. The signal means that the vehicle behind should follow the police car and stop when the police car stops.

soru: What does the police signal mean?
secenekler: Stop for vehicles facing the police and for vehicles behind the police
Reduce speed
Stop for vehicles behind the police
Stop for vehicles facing the police
aciklama: The police officer holds a red reflector disc and waves it up and down or holds it still facing traffic. This is an absolute stop signal for vehicles approaching from the direction the police officer is facing. The disc or light is often used in darkness or reduced visibility to attract drivers' attention.

soru: What does the road marking in the right lane mean?
secenekler: I am approaching an intersection with give way or stop obligation
Overtaking is prohibited
My lane will merge with another further ahead
The road narrows further ahead
aciklama: The large hollow triangle on the road surface is advance information about give way or stop obligation. It warns you in advance that you will need to give way or stop at the upcoming intersection, so that you can adjust your speed in time.

soru: You are driving the green car. The red truck is parked at the roadside due to work. Is it allowed to cross the solid centre line to pass the truck?
secenekler: No, I must stop and wait until the truck is finished
Yes, if I do not block oncoming traffic
Yes, but only if I use hazard lights when passing
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, it is forbidden to cross solid lines, but if an obstacle on the road (e.g. a truck that is working) must be passed and there is no other alternative, it is allowed to cross the line. The truck that is working counts as an obstacle. You may pass as long as you do not endanger or block oncoming traffic.

soru: What does the line in the middle of the road mean?
secenekler: It is a warning for limited visibility, but the line may be crossed
Visibility is limited only in my direction of travel
It is a warning for limited visibility and the line must absolutely not be crossed
Visibility is limited only for oncoming traffic
aciklama: The line with long dashes and short gaps is a warning line. It warns of limited visibility due to a hill crest or sharp curve ahead. It is not illegal to cross the line, but due to the limited visibility, it is strongly recommended not to overtake or cross the line unless absolutely necessary.

soru: At which road marking is it forbidden to stop?
secenekler: Marking A
Marking B
Marking C
Marking A and C
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, yellow lines at the kerb have the following meanings: A: No stopping and no parking. B: No parking (you may stop to drop off passengers). C: The zigzag yellow line is a complement to the dashed yellow line and also indicates no parking. Since the question is about where it is forbidden to stop, the correct answer is A.

soru: Which road marking indicates a cycle crossing or cycle passage?
secenekler: A
B
C
D
aciklama: The meanings of the road markings: A: Pedestrian crossing. B: Cycle crossing or cycle passage (square dashed white lines). C: Road obstacle such as speed bump or hump. D: Variable lane (direction can change depending on traffic intensity). The correct answer is B.

soru: You are driving in the right lane. Is it allowed to turn left at the intersection?
secenekler: Yes, the lane arrows are only a recommendation
No, I must follow the lane arrows
aciklama: The lane arrows on the road indicate which direction each lane leads at the upcoming intersection. In the picture, the right lane shows only straight ahead or right turn. Additionally, the lanes are separated by a solid line. According to Swedish rules, it is mandatory to follow the lane arrows, so from the right lane you may not turn left.

soru: What does the line in the middle of the road mean?
secenekler: This is a solid line
It marks the centre of the carriageway
It is forbidden to cross the line
The line may only be crossed to avoid a dangerous situation
aciklama: The short dashed lines in the picture are a normal centre line. According to Swedish traffic rules, it marks the centre of the carriageway and separates traffic in opposite directions. It is allowed to cross this line safely and in accordance with the rules.

soru: Which road marking is shown in the picture?
secenekler: Warning line
Edge line
Prohibited area / Hatched area
Variable lane
aciklama: The double dashed lines in the picture are the marking for 'Variable lane'. In these lanes, the traffic direction can change depending on the time of day or traffic intensity, and which direction applies is controlled by traffic lights above the lane.

soru: What is the maximum speed you may drive with a light lorry on a motorway with a 110 km/h limit?
secenekler: 80 km/h
90 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, light lorries have the same speed limits as passenger cars. Therefore, you may drive at the same speed as applies to the road, in this case 110 km/h.

soru: What is the maximum speed that moped class I is designed for?
secenekler: 20 km/h
25 km/h
35 km/h
45 km/h
aciklama: Mopeds are divided into two classes. Moped class I are registered vehicles designed for a maximum speed of 45 km/h and may be driven on main roads in a similar way to passenger cars. Moped class II is designed for a maximum of 25 km/h. The question concerns class I, so the correct answer is 45 km/h.

soru: Ahead of you, a vehicle with an LGF sign is driving. What is the maximum speed this vehicle may be driven at?
secenekler: 30 km/h
40 km/h
45 km/h
60 km/h
aciklama: The LGF sign (triangle) is used on slow vehicles to warn other road users. The maximum permitted speed for vehicles with an LGF sign is 45 km/h.

soru: What is the maximum speed for a heavy lorry on a state road with a 90 km/h limit?
secenekler: 60 km/h
70 km/h
80 km/h
90 km/h
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, the maximum permitted speed for heavy lorries on state roads is 80 km/h, regardless of whether the road's signposted speed is 90 km/h or higher. However, 90 km/h is permitted on motorways and motorway-like roads.

soru: What is the maximum speed you may drive with a car with a braked trailer on a motorway?
secenekler: 70 km/h
80 km/h
100 km/h
110 km/h
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, the maximum permitted speed for passenger cars with a braked trailer (or light trailer that meets certain conditions) is always 80 km/h, regardless of the road's signposted speed. This also applies on motorways.

soru: Which is correct?
secenekler: I may not drive faster than 80 km/h with a light lorry
I may not drive faster than 30 km/h when towing another vehicle
Buses may always drive at the speed that applies to the road, regardless of weight
aciklama: According to Swedish traffic rules, the maximum permitted speed when towing with a rope or tow bar is 30 km/h. The other alternatives are incorrect: light lorries have the same speed limits as passenger cars, and heavy buses with a total weight over 3.5 tonnes have a maximum speed of 90 km/h even on motorways.
